# Facts on record: history

## Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-09-19 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- **Boxing is not the ceiling on the scalar loop** (measured 2026-09-15, `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`; an edge case, see the entry above): on the 20 M-iteration scalar loop, compiled Fortress is 156× primitive Java, and a Java loop boxed the way the runtime boxes is 2.4-4.2× primitive, so boxing explains about 2% of the gap. The gap is three named, separately fixable costs: each float literal is rebuilt per iteration through `FFloatLiteral`, which stores the literal as a `String` and parses it back (about 30%); the accumulator's read and write go through `BaseTask.inATransaction()`, which builds a debug message eagerly on every call (about 34%, a one-line fix); the sequential `for` is `countedseqloop`, a recursive subdivision with boxed indices and a closure call per element (`CompilerLibrary.fss:340-348`, about 7%); the representational rest (volatile cell, allocations, interface hops, checkcasts) is about 30%. Interpreter/compiled 5.6× on this loop, 8.6× on the allocation loop. Ledger row 302; row 303 (kernels) corrects the general claim: on array code boxing is 6.3-6.5× in the Java models, so this bullet holds for the scalar loop only.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- The compiled path measured 6.8× on a scalar `RR64` loop, 8.9× on object-allocating code, 8× on startup, numerics identical (`compiled-path-gaps.md:45, 100-101`); what blocks it is its 592-line prelude (no `List`, no generic `array`, no `exp`/`log`, no `SUM`, an empty `Matrix`), not code generation (rows 71-82).

## What the conformance review of the eight rungs established (2026-09-17, `reviews/rung-conformance-1-4.md` and `-5-8.md`, verified in this session)

<!-- moved 2026-09-19 from FACTS.md § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established -->
- **A top-level mutable variable compiled by rung 3 is outside the transaction.** `VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding` reads and writes it with a bare `GETSTATIC`/`PUTSTATIC` on a non-final, non-volatile static field, while the team's own `LocalMutableVar` and `MutableTaskVarCodeGen` in the same file call `BaseTask.inATransaction()` and route through `TXRead`/`TXWrite` over a `volatile` cell, and the interpreter stores the same construct in a transactional `ReferenceCell` (`BaseEnv.java:599-601`). `atomic do ... end` does compile on this path with a real retry loop (`CodeGen.forAtomicBlock`), so such a variable is not in the write set, is not rolled back on abort and is written again by the retry, against `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:37-42` and `:65-67`. The gate cannot see it: every compiled atomic test uses a local variable and every `testSystem` shard pins `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established -->
- The review's first finding, a top-level mutable variable compiled outside the transaction, has been repaired: what the compiled path does now is the repair-batch entry in the ladder section below, the finding as it stood is in `FACTS-history.md` § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established, and the gate rule it exposed is the thread-count entry in that same section (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/REPORT.md`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established -->
- **The team already folds `IntLiteral` arithmetic at compile time and warned against doing it at run time.** `IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java` folds the operators in `BigInteger` and `phases/PhaseOrder.java:57,142` wires `INTEGERLITERALFOLDING` before `TYPECHECK`; three lines below the comparison block rung 6 cited by line number, `FortressBuiltin.fss` carries the team's comment, verbatim: "Do not enable these until coercion is implemented; doing so will cause all our arithmetic to occur on IntLiterals". Rung 7's run-time bodies are nonetheless genuinely needed, because folding is syntactic and cannot see a literal bound to a variable, which is the case its three files hit; what it landed without was the knowledge that the phase exists, so the throwing bodies read as unfinished work rather than as the bodies of a case the team meant to be folded away, and the two mechanisms now disagree on the same values: `println (4294967295 + 1)` folds to the correct `4294967296` while the same arithmetic through two variables gives `0`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What the conformance review of the eight rungs established -->
- **The specification makes an integer literal arbitrary precision** (`basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-85`, a digits-only numeral having the value of the numeral interpreted in radix ten, with nothing bounding it), and gives wrapping its own operator spellings (`basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:369-370, 400-401`), so the literal wrap of ledger row 317 is a violation predating the ladder rather than an unaddressed case.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § Earlier performance work on record -->
- **Checked integer arithmetic keeps integer loops scalar on the JVM** (2026-09-17, from the rung 6 skeptic's overflow finding; recorded at length in `performance-roadmap.md` under "Corrections recorded on the way"): `+` on `ZZ32` binds to `jIntOverflowingAdd` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:625`), whose helper (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntArith.java`) tests the sign bits and throws `IntegerOverflow`, which the spec mandates (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:114-117`; `⊞`/BOXPLUS is the wrapping operator, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:626`); HotSpot's SuperWord vectorizes only counted loops with no control flow in the body, so a branch per operation, however cheap scalar, forecloses SIMD. The consequence for the roadmap: step A5's "SIMD comes free from HotSpot" holds for floating-point loops, which is where microGPT's hot arithmetic is (`RR64`, no trapping), and not for the integer indices, counters and reductions around them, nor for A2's address arithmetic. Four remedies exist, cheapest first, and the roadmap lists them; none is worth doing before the loops are measured.

## What an autonomous climb costs in wall clock (measured 2026-09-17, `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md`)

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What an autonomous climb costs in wall clock -->
- **The eight-rung climb took 8h37m and every minute of it was serial**: 36 agents, no two ever overlapping, the sum of agent walls plus the 35 inter-agent gaps equalling the span exactly. Of the 508.3 agent-minutes, 57.8% was inside tool calls and 42.2% was model thinking, so no build optimization can buy back more than 57% of anything. The gate (`ant testFast` 14 runs at a 434 s median, `ant testSystem` 11 at 147.6 s) was 130.5 minutes, 25.2% of the clock; the ladder subset runs 64.9 and the library-order bytecode-cache rebuilds 44.6. `ant compileAll` ran exactly three times, in exactly the three rungs that touched `.java`/`.scala`, incremental at 46 s, and no cache rebuild ran over a still-valid cache: that discipline held. 41.0 minutes of gate produced no information, 21.7 of it because an agent piped `ant` through `tail` and had to re-run to see the summary it was required to grep, and 19.3 because a skeptic re-gated a byte-identical tree it had no mechanism to prove was fresh.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What an autonomous climb costs in wall clock -->
- **`ant testFast` cannot be made much faster by parallelism on this box**: its four tracks already occupy the four cores, one suite (`OtherCompilerJUTest`, 439.6 s) sets its wall, and the two gate targets run together have a realistic optimum of about 554 s against 583 s serial, 29 seconds, while sharing `test-caches`, `test-tmp` and `TEST-RESULTS` so they would need a `build.xml` change to be safe at all. Whole rungs in parallel worktrees buy nothing for the same reason: cores, not disk, are the constraint (a worktree costs 293 MB). What overlaps is a model-bound stage against a tool-bound one — `plan` is 68% model time and `implement` 76% tool.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § What an autonomous climb costs in wall clock -->
- **The three-component bytecode-cache rebuild is 4.7× the five-component one** where the edit is downstream of `AnyType` and `CompilerBuiltin`: 24.6-30.4 s against 110-162 s, found by the rung 8 agents in the climb's last hour after 20 of 22 rebuilds had used the long form.

## A user grammar on the compile path (measured 2026-09-16, `perf-probes/grammar-compile/REPORT.md`)

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § A user grammar on the compile path -->
- As shipped, a grammar-importing program stops at DISAMBIGUATE on the compile path with 1,342 errors, none in the program: every grammar api imports `FortressSyntax`, which imports `FortressAst`, which imports the interpreter's `FortressLibrary`, so the two preludes collide. The GRAMMAR phase is in the compiler's phase order and `GraphRepository.syntaxExpand` serves both worlds; what is missing is a compiler-world spelling of `FortressAst`/`FortressSyntax`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § A user grammar on the compile path -->
- With two probe-only shims shadowing `FortressLibrary` and `List` on the source path, the collision is gone, Rats! runs under `fortress compile`, and a user grammar compiles to bytecode and runs (`twicep⦇ 21 ⦈` prints 42).

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § A user grammar on the compile path -->
- Behind that wall the type checker does not know templates: there is no `TemplateGap`/`_SyntaxTransformation` case anywhere under `scala_src/typechecker/`. Consequences: an expansion in argument position must be parenthesized by the template text itself (`Argument to function must be parenthesized`); a template naming a function declared in the using component (ledger row 270, the mechanism the focused base's named functions rest on) crashes the post-typecheck assertion (`ClassCastException: BoxedUnit cannot be cast to AbstractNode`); a typed lambda written in a template (row 285) fails with `Unbound type: ZZ32`, the type never disambiguated. So rows 270, 282 and 285, the APL ladder's whole division of labour, are interpreter-only facts, and the APL microGPT cannot go through the compiler until the checker learns templates. Ledger rows 288-291 (merged 2026-09-16).

- 410 files (381 `ProjectFortress/tests/` plus 29 `not_working_library_tests/`) through `fortress compile` and `fortress run` unchanged, 11.5 minutes, private cache. `tests/`: parse 1, disambiguate 148, typecheck 141, codegen 21, link 4, run 10, pass 56. `not_working_library_tests/`: parse 14, disambiguate 9, typecheck 2, link 1, pass 3. 289 of 381 stop before codegen: the gap is library and checker, not codegen.

Cascade names (failing inside an imported api such as `Library/List.fsi`): `Maybe` 50, `Comprehension` 48, `BigReduction` 48, `MonoidReduction` 48, `HasRank` 41, `LexicographicOrder` 37, `ImmutableArray` 29, `Array` 29, `Equality` 24, `ZeroIndexed` 23, `StandardTotalOrder` 22.

<!-- moved 2026-09-19 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **Rung 1, `Equality`, landed** (2026-09-17, `compile-ladder/rung1/REPORT.md`): four edits in four files put `CompilerAlgebra` into the compiler world's implicit prelude — `WellKnownNames.java:124` uncommented, one branch added to the disambiguator's own hard-coded implicit list at `TopLevelEnv.java:967-976` (the set is written down twice and only that copy decides what a program sees), the private `trait Equality` deleted from `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss`, and the checker's `FunctionalRef` case in `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala` narrowed to the static arguments written at the reference site. That last one is ledger row 311 and the hypothesis on record was wrong: the kind-environment crash is not in `TypeAnalyzer.comprisedTypes` but in the well-formedness walk of synthesized overloading types, which carry a generic declaration's own static parameters free (`= newOverloadings=14`, one of them `(((CompilerAlgebra.Equality[\T\] & {T}), T)->Boolean)`). `library_tests/EqualityRung1` and `compiler_tests/Compiled9` pass, `ant testFast` (47 suites) and `ant testSystem` (4 shards) are at zero failures and zero errors, and the 23-file subset reproduces the measured route byte for byte: all clear `Equality`, none moves down, two advance to typecheck (`EqualityOverloadBug`, `GS3`) and 21 stop on the next name in disambiguate (`ImmutableArray` 20, `Maybe` 1), so `ImmutableArray` is the same file set one name on and the ranking's head must be re-derived from a fresh ladder run. The ladder's pass count is unchanged at 59. The fallback of declaring `Equality` in `CompilerLibrary` stays refuted (ambiguity with `CompilerAlgebra` takes 14 errors on each of the five library components), and `=/=` on a user type is still a separate name: the compiler world has no `opr =(Any,Any)` and no `opr =/=(Any,Any)`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-19 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **Rung 2, `HasRank`, landed** (2026-09-17, `compile-ladder/rung2/REPORT.md`): one trait declared in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi` and `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`, `trait HasRank extends Equality[\HasRank\] excludes { Number }` with `abstract rank(): ZZ32` in the api and `rank(): ZZ32` in the component, in the spelling of `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1058` / `.fss:1584` minus two things the compiler world has no referent for: `AnyMaybe` in the excludes clause, and the interpreter's `opr =(self, other:HasRank): Boolean = false`, so `HasRank` takes the `opr =` that rung 1's now-implicit `CompilerAlgebra.Equality` supplies. No Java or Scala change and no checker work: `extends Equality[\HasRank\]` passes the `comprises T` rule that rung 1 had to work around, because `HasRank` is itself the `T`. The head of the baseline ranking was re-derived first — `Equality`'s 23 files had become `ImmutableArray` 20 + `Maybe` 1, putting `ImmutableArray` at about 26 first-error files against `HasRank`'s 21, but `ImmutableArray` is not takeable without choosing the array representation (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1870` declares it over `Range`, `TrivialOpenRange`, `Indexed` and `Generator`, and `CovariantCollection.fss` implements `toImmutableArray`/`toArray`/`assignToArray` against a backing store), which is a reserved fork; by the cascade ranking `HasRank` (41 files) is the wider name anyway. `library_tests/HasRankRung2` passes, `ant testFast` (47 suites, 1,381 tests, `LibraryJUTest` 57 → 59) and `ant testSystem` (4 shards, 382 tests) are at zero failures and zero errors, and the 21-file subset moves up with nothing moving down: all 21 clear `HasRank`, 20 stay in disambiguate and stop on `LexicographicOrder` at `Library/List.fsi:67`, and `tests/oddJuxt.fss` clears `test_library/oddJuxtComp.fsi` entirely and stops on its own line 22. The ladder's pass count is unchanged at 59. `LexicographicOrder` reaches `StandardTotalOrder` (present, `CompilerAlgebra.fsi:16`) and `ZeroIndexed` → `Indexed` → `Generator` (absent), so it is its own and larger rung; the ranking's head after this rung must again be re-derived from a fresh ladder run.

<!-- moved 2026-09-19 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **Rung 3, top-level mutable variable bindings in the code generator, landed** (2026-09-17, `compile-ladder/rung3/REPORT.md`): two Java edits and no library, checker or Scala change. `CodeGen.forVarDeclPrePass` (`CodeGen.java:5891`) threw `VarDecl … mutable bindings not yet handled.` for both `var v: T = e` and `v: T := e`, while the same declaration inside a block already worked (`forLocalVarDecl` builds a `VarCodeGen.LocalMutableVar`); the refusal is dropped, the mutability is threaded into `generateVarDeclInnerClass` so the variable's singleton field is emitted `ACC_PUBLIC+ACC_STATIC` without `ACC_FINAL` (the JVM forbids a `PUTSTATIC` to a final field from outside the declaring class), and a new `VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding` — `GETSTATIC` to read, `PUTSTATIC` to write — is registered in place of `StaticBinding`, whose `assignValue` keeps throwing so assignment to an immutable top-level variable still fails. No new initialization mechanism was needed: one inner class per top-level variable means the JVM's demand-driven `<clinit>` already gives dependency order, which `tests/InitOrderWithMutable.fss` (`bvar = cvar` before `var cvar: String = avar`) confirms by printing `PASS`. `compiler_tests/MutableTopLevelVar` passes, `ant testFast` (48 suites) and `ant testSystem` (4 shards, 382 tests) are at zero failures and zero errors, and all eight subset files go from the refusal to a clean compile and a clean run — the first rung of this climb to move the ladder's pass count, **59 to 67**. Ledger row 312. - **An integer literal of `bitLength` exactly 32 or exactly 64 is wrapped negative by the code generator** (2026-09-17, ledger row 317, `compiler-probes/p37.fss` and `p37a.fss` run both ways, outputs at `compile-ladder/rung6/probes/`): `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` (`CodeGen.java:3859-3893`) splits on `BigInteger.bitLength()` and sends `<= 32` through `intValue()` and `<= 64` through `longValue()`, but `bitLength()` of a non-negative `BigInteger` carries no sign bit, so `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` are each stored as `-1` while only `bitLength() > 64` keeps the decimal string; the author's comment on the line above the split is "This might not work". Through a declared binding the divergence predates rung 6 -- `a: ZZ64 = 4294967295`, `b: ZZ64 = 5`, walk `false`, compiled `true`, by way of `ZZ64.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:557`) -- so annotating the binding is not a workaround and none is known; through an undeclared binding it is what rung 6 opened, where the stub threw before. No library edit repairs it, `asZZ` included, because the wrap precedes every getter; the repair is in `forIntLiteralExpr`, whose decimal-string branch does not wrap and whose two narrow branches need the signed range rather than `bitLength`. Same class as row 79, the silent compiled-against-interpreter disagreement, reached through the literal's value instead of `typecase`. Rung 7 widened it from comparison to arithmetic: `a = 4294967295`, `b = 1`, `println (a + b)` gives walk `4294967296` and compiled `0` (`compile-ladder/rung7/probes/p39.fss`). **Repaired by R2 of the repair batch** (the rung's work of 2026-09-18, landed on `main` 2026-09-19 as `6a63980b`), whose entries below state what the compiled path does now; this bullet describes the tree up to `49ee5e91`.

- **The compiler prelude has `MOD`, `REM`, `GCD`, `LCM`, `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT` on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, in pure Fortress and with no native helper** (rung N, 2026-09-19, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integral-ops/REPORT.md`): twelve declarations at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:176-179`, `:196-197` (`ZZ64`) and `:237-240`, `:257-258` (`ZZ32`), and twelve bodies at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:584-606`, `:630-631` (`ZZ64`) and `:667-689`, `:717-718` (`ZZ32`). `REM` is the specification's own identity `m REM n = m - n(m ÷ n)` (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:484`) over the trait's `DIV`, `-` and juxtaposition, so it inherits `DIV`'s `DivisionByZero`, with one guard: the divisor `-1` returns `0` directly, because `x REM -1` is `0` for every `x` while `MIN DIV -1` overflows legitimately on a fixed-size type and the gated corpus pins that it must (`ProjectFortress/library_tests/Integer3.fss:127`, `Integer4.fss:127`). `MOD` is `REM` with the interpreter's four-branch sign correction (`glue/prim/Int.java:307-318`); `GCD` is Euclid over `REM` in the `var`/`while` shape `trait ZZ`'s own `CHOOSE` already uses (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:538-552`), normalized to nonnegative at the end; `LCM` is over `GCD` and `DIV`; `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT` are names for the `<<` and `>>` of the same trait. `MOD` and `GCD` reach the `-1` guard through `REM`, so one guard covers all three. Gated by `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntegralOpsRungN.{fss,test}`, which pins all four sign combinations of `REM` and `MOD` against the specification's table (`basic-integers.tex:465-468`), the `GCD`/`LCM` prose (`:523-529`), the lattice property (`:544`), the shifts against `<<`/`>>`, division by zero, the divisor `-1` and the type minimum for `REM`, `MOD` and `GCD` on both `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, the two boundary cases whose true result is `2^31` and which therefore must throw, and twenty-two `ZZ64` cases beyond `ZZ32`. `NN32` and `NN64` were deliberately left out.

- **The gate's thread count is inherited from the shell, and this repository pins it to one.** The chain is: the `fastTrack` macro that runs `compiler_tests` sets `FORTRESS_CACHES` and no thread count and no `newenvironment` (`build.xml:927-953`), so the forked JUnit JVM inherits the ambient environment; the harness runs each program in a further subprocess that inherits again (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:480-486`); and `FortressExecutable.getNumThreads` reads `FORTRESS_THREADS` first and only falls back to the processor count or `floor(n/2)` when it is unset (`:37-44`). `experiment/env.sh:6` exports `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, every rung brief tells the agent to source it, and `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md:126` records that no run in the climb used anything else — so in the gate as this project runs it, `compiler_tests` gets one worker. Measured consequence: `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` passes on the *unrepaired* base tree at one thread (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/skeptic-basetree.txt`, `BASE run AtomicTopLevelVar THREADS=1 :: PASS`), so it is vacuous there and the two deterministic tests are what carry R1. The `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` in the `testSystem` shards (`build.xml:1184`) is a second, explicit pin on a corpus this does not concern. A concurrency defect on the compiled path is therefore **not** gateable by a concurrent test as the gate stands; it is gateable only by a test that fails at one thread. (This line replaces the claim R1 first offered, that `compiler_tests` runs with more than one worker: the chain was right as far as it went and stopped one line short of `getNumThreads`'s first statement.)

- **The transaction runtime built twenty-two of its twenty-three disabled debug messages eagerly, and on the transactional path that was a crash, not only a cost.** `Transaction.java` has fourteen `debug(` call sites and `BaseTask.java` nine; each concatenated its argument before `debug(String)` tested the flag, except `BaseTask.java:248`, which rung 0 of this same climb had already guarded. Nine of `Transaction.java`'s sites stringify a Fortress value or a table of them, which for an object or trait value with no `asString` of its own enters the `FValue.toString` / `CompilerBuiltin.fss:338` / `stringOps.java:38-40` cycle (ledger row 321) and overflows the stack. Once R1 routed a top-level mutable variable's accesses through the transaction, a twelve-line single-threaded program that ran on `49ee5e91` died (`probes/skeptic/SK25ObjNoAtomicVsAtomic.fss`, frames in `sk25-recursion-entry.txt`). All twenty-three call sites now carry the `if (debug)` guard, twenty-two of them applied in R1's repair round (2026-09-19) in the idiom `BaseTask.java:248` already used, and the case is gated by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, whose object type deliberately declares no `asString`. The per-access cost this removes is the mechanism ledger row 302 measured at about 34 % of a 156× gap: inside a transaction each read and write had been building a discarded string of the value (`Transaction.java:162,166,227`), each commit rendering both hash tables (`:232`) and every entry (`:249`), and `BaseTask.getCurrentTransaction` (`:234`) a `Thread` on every call.

- **A radix numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern, and the compile path was the only place that pretended otherwise.** `literals.tex:104-108` gives a radix numeral the type `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]]` over the value of its digits in radix $r$, so `8000'0000_16` is $2^{31}$ and `A0000000_16` is $2684354560$; the interpreter has always refused such a numeral at a signed type ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32"), and the compile path accepted it only because the wrap turned it into something else. Five sites in the tree relied on that: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` (`ZZ32_MIN`, `ZZ64_MIN`), `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46` (`twiceHuge`), and `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:115` (`:114` before R2's own added binding) with its ungated twin `ChooseTest3.fss:125`. The first four are repaired value-for-value; the fifth was not only illegal but was exercising `i = -1257966796` instead of the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment names (2026-09-19, R2 of the repair batch, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).

So the criterion for "new file or the team's file" is that one: a helper over primitives belongs in the existing `simple*Arith.java` of its type, a helper over a Fortress value needs its own file and its own clause.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **One Fortress scope cannot hold both spellings of an optional type's empty case, and the non-parametric declaration wins the name silently.** Declaring `value object NothingD[\T extends Any\] extends MaybeD[\T\]` and then `value object NothingD end` in one component does not raise a duplicate-name error: the name resolves with zero static parameters, and it is the *parametric* declaration's own header and the `comprises` clause naming it that become errors — "Incorrect number of static arguments for type 'NothingD': provided 1, expected 0" (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/DualNothing.fss`, `.txt`). So an optional type's empty case is a binary choice, with no overload that serves both spellings, and a tree that mixes them fails at the parametric uses rather than at the declarations.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **`Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` are named from Java after all, in `syntax_abstractions/`, which is outside the `compiler/` + `runtimeSystem/` scope the climb has been grepping.** `syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117` builds an **unqualified** `Maybe[\X\]` trait type for a grammar template variable of option depth (`NodeFactory.makeId(span, "Maybe")`), and `syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58` maps the name texts `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`, each with exactly one type argument, to the Java `Option<arg>`; `FortressTypeToJavaTypeJUTest.java:60-94` is that mapping's unit test, and the interpreter's `Evaluator.java:595` compares a typecase clause's type name against `"Just"`. Being unqualified, they resolve against whatever `WellKnownNames.useCompilerLibraries()` points the prelude at (`WellKnownNames.java:113-115`), so before this rung an option-depth gap referred to an undeclared `Maybe` on the compile path and now it resolves — the direction the design intends, since the name was chosen for the interpreter prelude's `Maybe`. It cannot break: that code reads only the name text and the argument count, and `Maybe[\T extends Any\]` takes the one argument it expects. It also cannot reach the gate, though not for the reason a grep of the compile-path corpora gives: `grep -rln 'grammar '` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` finds no file, but those three are not the only gated corpus — `syntax_abstraction_tests/` is driven by `SyntaxAbstractionJUTest`, which `testFast` does run (`build.xml:974` includes `**/*JUTest.class` in the `misc` track and `:987` excludes only `SyntaxAbstractionJUTestAll`). The reason is the phase order: that suite runs `ForUse.fss` and its siblings through `StaticTestSuite.StaticTestCase` (`SyntaxAbstractionJUTest.java:31,41`), whose `compile()` sets `Shell.setPhaseOrder(PhaseOrder.interpreterPhaseOrder)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticTestSuite.java:334`), so it never loads `CompilerLibrary` and never sees this rung's declarations. **The general lesson for later rungs**: "nothing in Java or Scala names this" must be grepped over `src/com/sun/fortress/` and not over `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` alone.

- **A binary operator applied to two integer literals resolves by coercion, and the expected type at the call site picks the trait — unless `trait IntLiteral` declares that operator itself, in which case its own overload wins** (rung N, 2026-09-19, probes at `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integral-ops/probes/`): `3 << 4` answers `48` although `<<` is declared four times over on each of four numeric traits (`probes/LitResolve2.fss`), `t(3 << 4, 48)` with `t(x:ZZ32, y:ZZ32)` and `u(3 << 4, 48)` with `u(x:ZZ64, y:ZZ64)` both pass (`probes/LitTarget.fss`), and `3 BITAND 4` throws `CompilerFailureDetectedAtRunTime` from rung 7's stub at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:895` (`probes/LitResolve2.fss`). The folding phase is not involved: `desugarer/IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java:105-106` returns the node untouched for every operator outside its list, and `MOD`, `REM`, `GCD`, `LCM`, `<<` and `>>` are all outside it. The consequence for prelude work: a name that literal-literal call sites use must **not** be declared on `IntLiteral` unless it can be given a real body there. The interpreter world reached the same conclusion first and left the evidence in place: all six of these operators are written out on `object IntLiteral` at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:501-508` and `:517-520` (api `FortressBuiltin.fsi:130-133`, `:138-139`) inside a comment that opens at `.fss:483` and reads "Do not enable these until coercion is implemented; doing so will cause all our arithmetic to occur on IntLiterals" (`:484-485`).

- **The harness's freed slots go to the next worker, not to the finished worker's skeptic, so a rung's verdict arrives long after the rung** (2026-09-19, the journal of `wf_3b5a273c-a80`, agent start and end times parsed with `repair-batch-review/parse.py`): the harness runs two agents at a time, and CLIMB-BATCH-1 predicted "two waves"; the run was four. `rung:F` ended 08:38:38 and the slot went to `rung:N` at 08:38:40, not to `skeptic:F`; `rung:M` ended 08:41:06 and the slot went to `rung:T` at 08:41:09. `skeptic:F` did not start until 09:20:50, **42 min 12 s after the rung it judges finished**, and `skeptic:M` until 09:22:59. The consequence is structural rather than incidental: `skeptic:N`'s refusal, which forced the judge-repair-skeptic chain, could not have arrived before 09:36 under this order although `rung:N` finished at 09:20, and from 09:53:21 to the end at 11:44:15 — 110.9 of the run's 200.1 minutes, 55 % — exactly one agent was running. Overall concurrency was 1.43× (285.6 agent-minutes over a 200.1-minute span) against the repair batch's 1.21×. A schedule that gave a freed slot to the finished rung's skeptic first would have overlapped each refusal's repair chain with the remaining rungs.

- **The four integer conversions are in the compiler prelude** (2026-09-20, rung W of climb batch 2, `compile-ladder/rung-int-conversions/REPORT.md`). `widen`, `narrow`, `unsigned` and `signed` are declared on the four fixed-size integer traits: `widen` and `unsigned` on `trait ZZ32`, `narrow` and `unsigned` on `trait ZZ64`, `widen` and `signed` on `trait NN32`, `narrow` and `signed` on `trait NN64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:206-207`, `:269-270`, `:328-329`, `:386-387`, bodies at `.fss:654-655`, `:745-746`, `:810-811`, `:874-875`). `widen` sign-extends from `ZZ32` and zero-extends from `NN32`; `unsigned` and `signed` reinterpret the bits, so `unsigned(-1)` is 4294967295 and `signed` of it is -1; `narrow` throws `IntegerOverflow` when the value does not fit, on both the signed and the unsigned side — a decision, argued in the rung's report and carried as ledger row 346. `NN64.signed` is declared returning `ZZ64`, not the `NN64` the interpreter's api writes (row 345). Gated by `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntConversionsRungW.fss` (47 assertions) and `.test`. Not added, by name: `partitionL`, `partition`, `big`, `RR64.narrow(): RR32`, and `narrow`/`widen` on `trait ZZ`, which the interpreter declares at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:539-540` (row 349). One transition the rung did not report and the gather measured: `narrow(z)` for `z: ZZ32` now compiles and is a silent identity, reached by coercion through `ZZ64.coerce(x: ZZ32)` at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:575`, 43 in and 43 out on both paths (`probes/gather/gather-narrow-zz32.txt`).

## The syntax-extension mechanism (the APL ladder's findings, ledger 179-287; narrative in `apl/lessons.md`)

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The syntax-extension mechanism -->
- A binder written literally in a template is renamed by hygiene; a free name written by another template is not; they never meet (row 204); an `Id` gap in a binder position is not renamed (row 201). Consequence: a sub-language cannot type or even name `⍵` inside a user-written body; named functions and lambdas one rule writes whole are the two shapes that work (rows 285, 96 of `apl/gaps.md`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The syntax-extension mechanism -->
- The interpreter refuses every nested re-declaration of a name (rung 4 probes u01-u03); with hygiene this is why rung 4 built a frame stack, which is unsafe under implicit parallelism (row 265) and was replaced by the focused base (`apl/mg/`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The syntax-extension mechanism -->
- APL names are closed sets, one grammar line per name (row 194, 202); a word of two or more capitals is an operator, not a name (row 7/193).

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The syntax-extension mechanism -->
- A host `Expr` gap swallows a following terminal that is a host operator (`⋄`, `∘`) (row 284); a template that writes the host caret drops its right operand silently (row 286); nine `apl⦇ ⦈` uses in one expression do not parse (row 261); parser generation costs about 15-40 s per grammar-importing run.

<!-- moved 2026-09-20 from FACTS.md § The syntax-extension mechanism -->
- Direct rules cost 3.8× less than general forms with per-element frame pushes (row 256); with per-row or per-plane cells the general route was 1.12× C4 at pool 1 and 1.49× at pool 4; the focused base is level with C4 at both.

### Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- **On microGPT-shaped code, boxing is the dominant representational cost, and nothing microGPT-shaped runs on the compiled path today** (measured 2026-09-15, `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`, which corrects the boxing probe's scalar-loop conclusion below as Pavol suspected): the three kernels the program is made of (a 4192-element dot product, a 16×16 matrix product, the row lift with `rmsn`) all fail to compile with `Array is undefined`, `Vector is undefined`, `Array3 is undefined` in `FlatArrays.fsi` (77 errors): the compiler prelude lacks the array TYPES, not only the constructor (wider than ledger row 72; ledger row 305). In Java models of those kernels, boxing as the runtime boxes costs 6.3× (dot), 6.5× (matrix), 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`, because array element results escape and cannot be scalar-replaced; the generic array object adds only 1.6-9% on top. On the interpreter, the only path that runs them, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch, 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). A fairly written scalar loop (literals hoisted, no `:=`) compiles to 9.7× primitive Java; JFR on the real compiled run puts 88.9% of the mutable-variable loop under `BaseTask.inATransaction()`'s eagerly built debug string (`BaseTask.java:248`, `Thread.toString()` through `StringBuilder`). Order that follows: (1) an `RR64` array type in the compiler library (G2) so the kernels exist on that path; (2) the two one-line defects, the debug string and `FFloatLiteral`'s String round-trip; (3) unboxing and `double[]`, where the remaining ~6× on array code lives, designed into (1) rather than retrofitted. Also: a local function does not compile (`Can't compile LetFn`, `CodeGen.java:1552`, ledger row 304); a failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache.

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- Rung 0's two fixes took the eager debug string (row 302) and `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip (row 303) out of the scalar loop, so the boxing probe's own reading of the unrepaired tree — 156× primitive Java, of which boxing was about 2 %, with `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7 %) and the representational rest (about 30 %) still unaddressed — is history (`FACTS-history.md` § Execution model; `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- **The two one-line runtime defects are fixed** (2026-09-17, rung 0 of the plan, `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, `before.out`/`after.out`): guarding `BaseTask.inATransaction()`'s debug message with the `debug` flag it already had (`BaseTask.java:248`, ledger row 302) takes the compiled `bench1h`, the loop whose literals are hoisted so the transaction check is the only defect left in it, from **8.8159 s to 0.7287 s** (loop-only medians of 3, JDK 25, 20 M iterations, same freshly rebuilt library jars on both sides).

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- **Caching the `double` in `FFloatLiteral`** instead of keeping the literal as a `String` and re-parsing it in `asRR64()` (ledger row 303) takes the compiled `bench1t`, which builds both float literals inside the loop, from **13.0566 s to 0.7384 s**; the literals' own share, the `bench1t` minus `bench1h` difference, falls from 4.2407 s to 0.0097 s, so the per-iteration decimal round trip is gone (2026-09-17, `compile-ladder/rung0/`). The gate after both edits: `ant testFast` 1,377 tests, `ant testSystem` 382 tests, zero failures and zero errors.

### The compile-path ladder baseline (2026-09-17, `explorations/compile-ladder/REPORT.md`)

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **The ladder's measured pass count after climb batch 1 is 85 of 410** (2026-09-19, `compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`, a full run with the baseline's driver, commit `cb55877df`): 82 of 381 `tests` and 3 of 29 `not_working_library_tests`; eleven files move up and none down (M: `ExceptionScoping`, `oddJuxt` to typecheck; F: `buffons`, `juxtTwice`, `oprTests`, `roundBug` to typecheck; N: `chain0` to pass, `rshiftbug` to codegen; T: `nestedTransactions1/2/4` to pass); `pass-list.txt` is the ladder-regression stage's baseline. **All eighteen components of the two microGPT programs stop at disambiguate on four names**, `Array`, `Char`, `Vector`, `ImmutableArray` (`microgpt-phase.md`), the head of the ladder's own ranking and behind the array-representation fork; any one reaching the checker is a move.

<!-- moved 2026-09-24 from FACTS.md § The compile-path ladder baseline -->
- **`MicroGptFlatCheck` does not start from a cold interpreter cache** (2026-09-19, same report): the first run dies in `Shell.walk` with `FlatArrays.fss:31` `MAX[\I\](s:RR64, a:Array[\RR64,I\])` against `FortressLibrary.fss:280` `StandardTotalOrder[\T\].MAX`, "at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types" (`OverloadedFunction.java:527`), reproduced twice; the failed run leaves `FlatArrays` in `interpreter_cache`, a cached component is not re-checked, and the second run succeeds. Every C4 number on record was taken warm; a fresh container cannot run the check at the first attempt. **Investigated the same day** (`run-c4/cold-cache/`, rows 341 and 342): the pair is illegal under `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-105` (one declaration has static parameters and the other has none of its own) and under the meet rule of `advanced/overloading.tex:247-262`, so the defect is C4's, hidden since `FlatArrays` was written; the interpreter's verdict is right by a conservative test (`OverloadedFunction.java:452-456, 498-500`); a 13-line reproducer needs two generic declarations behind an api. `Shell.java:620` caches the component before `:621` runs the program, and `ComponentWrapper.populateOne:112` writes the second cache before the environment build at `:121` reaches the check; five ablations show the suppressor is `interpreter_parsed_cache/FortressLibrary*`, so the check runs only on a run that re-analyzes the library (refines row 98). Known and misjudged: `apl/mg/NOTES-swap.md:223-227` called the same failure "bogus" and said run twice. The fix is a rename at `FlatArrays.fss:31-32` and `FlatArrays2.fss:40-41`, Pavol's call. **Corrected the same evening by the FlatArrays review** (`reviews/c4-flatarrays-review.md`, evidence `run-c4/cold-cache/max-shapes/`, 26 probes each on its own empty cache): the rename is not the whole repair — `MAX` is one of four families the check refuses cold, with `+` (`FlatArrays.fss:24-25,134` against `AdditiveGroup.+`), `-` (`:26-27` against the library's ground `-` at `:4499`) and juxtaposition (`:42,126` against `MultiplicativeRing`); with `MAX` renamed or composed at the call site the same cold run dies on `+`, and `FlatArrays2` carries the same four families. The trigger is two or more declarations of one name with a trait-typed operand in the non-self position, ground or generic; one such declaration passes by the interpreter's accident, not by the specification. C4 uses the library's own `Array`/`Vector`/`Matrix`/`Array3` throughout, there is no flat-array type: of `FlatArrays.fsi`'s 40 names 5 are standard as they are, 26 are new operations over the standard types, 9 are view objects extending them; the library has no scalar extension for `RR64` arrays (`+ - MIN MAX` over `Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]` only, `FortressLibrary.fss:4493-4517`) and nothing elementwise at rank 3. A minimal in-place repair was built and measured (`max-shapes/H3/`): five declarations fewer, one model line changed, green on a cold cache at the first run, the five losses identical to C4's committed digits, 8.0 s per step as C4. The decision is Pavol's (options in the review §6). **Settled the same night by a second probe worker** (`run-c4/cold-cache/operators/`, routes A-D): the fix that changes zero lines of the model and is the library's own pattern is route C — the library's integer scalar-extension block (`FortressLibrary.fss:4493-4517`, `.fsi:2537-2540`) rewritten as eight generic declarations `opr +[\T extends Number, I\](x: Array[\T,I\], y: T)` and the mirror order, likewise `-`, `MIN`, `MAX` (precedent: the `T extends Number` array operators at `:2261-2276`, `:2621-2634`), plus route D's fifteen lines closing the tower and marking the traits: `trait AnyIntegral … comprises { ZZ }` (`:609`, the one open `comprises` link; the api already closes it at `.fsi:533`), the `AnyMultiplicativeRing` pattern (`:335-336`) applied to `AdditiveGroup`, and `Array3 … excludes { Number, String, AnyAdditiveGroup, AnyMultiplicativeRing }` (`:2666`). Under it C4 drops six scalar declarations and the `Diag` product (now the library's), `Diag` becomes a `Matrix` view, the plane-wise `+` and the batched juxtaposition stay one each, and `MicroGptFlat.fss` is byte-identical; cold from an empty cache the first run is 40 PASS with output identical to `checks/threads1.txt` (`operators/C/run1.txt`, `C.library.diff` 56 lines, `C.c4.diff` 35 lines). Why the integer block loads today: the interpreter makes a trait with a `comprises` clause exclude whatever every leaf object excludes (`FType.java:281-297`, `FTypeTrait.java:68-78`); `ZZ32`'s leaves are closed, `RR64`'s include the open `AnyIntegral`. ### Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- On microGPT-shaped array code boxing is the dominant representational cost, 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]` in Java models of the program's three kernels, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles: the compiler prelude lacks the array types, with `Array`, `Vector` and `Array3` undefined in `FlatArrays.fsi` (row 305, wider than row 72). On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The order that followed: an `RR64` array type in the compiler library (G2); the two one-line runtime defects (rows 302, 303, since fixed by rung 0); unboxing and `double[]`, designed into the first. A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`258105b3e`; `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`) (full entry in FACTS-history.md).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); whether `nat` parameters are baked into stamped classes is unprobed. Superseded 2026-09-24: a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`). A size's descriptor in a stamped class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` since climb batch 5 rung Z (`e893a3e00`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half). Its first sentence is superseded 2026-09-26 by climb batch 4 rung N (`3f297441c`): the compiled checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters ("The checker and the one library" below); a sized program still fails at load until the run-time rung. Its last clause, that a sized program still fails at load, is superseded by climb batch 5 rung Z (`e893a3e00`; "A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § Execution model -->
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`) gives the identical single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`'s "when we get where clauses working", and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way. Corrected 2026-09-26 (`reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothing.fss`, `SpecNothingNoExcludes.fss` and their captures): the probe of this entry (`WhereClauseNothing.fss:12`) left out the declaration's `excludes Just[\T\]`; written as the specification writes it, the declaration stops earlier on both paths with a syntax error at `excludes`, because the grammar gives an object no `excludes` clause (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:84-86`); `T is undefined` is what it gives once that clause is removed.

### The checker and the one library

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library -->
- `fortress compile Library/FortressLibrary.fss` as it is: 1,417 errors, all in DISAMBIGUATE, all name collisions because both preludes are in scope; an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` made the prelude (a driver over `Shell`'s public entry points, no tracked file changed): disambiguation passes with zero errors; the type checker then reports 92 errors in the library's own apis (36 `X excludes Y but it extends Y`, 26 `types exclude each other`, 26 `Integral[\I\]` bound failures, in the comparison and numeric tower) and then **crashes: `Not yet implemented`** in `STypesUtil.makeInferenceArg` (STypesUtil.scala:546-559) for `nat`, `int`, `bool`, `dim` and `unit` static parameters. Desugar and codegen are never reached. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16. Its crash is superseded 2026-09-26 by climb batch 4 rung N (`3f297441c`): the checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters, and a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` one is refused by name ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library -->
- **The Scala type checker does not implement `nat` static parameters at all**: a six-line program with a `nat` parameter fails on the compile path (`Not yet implemented` inferred, `ClassCastException` explicit) and runs on the interpreter. So the sized-array vocabulary cannot pass the compile path's checker today, and the static dimension checking the `nat` design promises is not implemented anywhere. Source: `perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md`, measured 2026-09-16. Superseded 2026-09-26 by climb batch 4 rung N (`3f297441c`) for `nat` and `int`, the entry "The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below; `bool`, `dim` and `unit` have a named error, not rules.

- **What a size costs at run time, measured: the designs differ by a few kilobytes at load and by nothing on the hot path, and only the overload dispatcher ever reads a size off a value** (2026-09-24, `perf-probes/nat/size-cost.md`, programs and captures under `perf-probes/nat/size-cost/`, on the size probes' stack with A and B runs interleaved; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md` revised the same day with a self-contained refresher on the run time's descriptor machinery, folding in the walkthrough's §§ 5, 6 and 8, and a section "Run-time cost, measured" answering Pavol's questions; its proposed default is now B, marked as not a decision). Start-up equal within noise (`pNat1` A 618/583/577 ms, B 598/665/571 ms). Hot loop (`SizedSum`, a sized object's method over eight elements, 10 M calls): the stamped method's bytecode is identical under A and B with the size the constant `ldc 8` (`k3b-javap.txt:41, 145-146`), times equal within 7 % with the lead flipping between rounds; bounding the loop by the constant size is no faster than reading the storage's length, because the cost is boxing and a transaction check per local variable, about 31 ns per element, and nothing ties the size to the storage's length (`k3-hotloop.out`). Dispatch: for literal-size arms both designs emit the same `instanceof` on the stamped class; for an arm generic in a size B reads the size's descriptor and looks the arm up in a table on every call, while A runs the catch-all (`k4-dispatch.out`, `k4b-javap.txt`); a dispatched call costs about 4-20 ns more than a resolved one, against a loop of 30-50 ns per call. - **The coercions between number types carry a sum's zero and a product's one into every wider type by themselves, and not a maximum's identity** (2026-09-26, `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement.md` §§ 1-2, probes and captures under `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement/`). A coercion keeps the arithmetic, so the converted zero and one are the wider type's own, measured on both paths: on walk with `widen`, for a `ZZ64` `y` below `ZZ32`'s range, `widen(0) + y` and `widen(1) y` give `y`, and into `RR64` `0 + (-1.0e300)` gives `-1.0e300` (`MaxMinWalk.walk.txt` § 5); compiled, where the coercion is real, `s: ZZ64 = SUM[j <- 0#0] j` holds `ZZ32`'s zero converted and `s + y` gives `y` (`MaxComp.comp.txt`). A maximum's identity is the type's least element (a minimum's its greatest), which a coercion does not carry: the smallest `ZZ32` widened, `MAX` `y`, gives -2147483648, not `y` (walk), and compiled `m: ZZ64 = BIG MAX[j <- 0#0] j` holds -2147483648 with `m MAX y = m`; `ZZ` and `QQ` have no least element. The library's generic `BIG MAX` has no identity, and an empty one raises `EmptyReduction`, which the team's test asserts (`ProjectFortress/tests/simpleSum.fss:56-60`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2907-2927`, `:3117-3147`); its one extremum with an identity is `BIG MAXNUM`/`BIG MINNUM`, `RR64` only, NaN. Under answer 7 the identity is made at the fold's own type, so no identity is coerced inside a reduction. The three `Number`-typed `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `BIG MINMAXN` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3076-3114`), whose identity is the rational `-1/0` for every element type and which have no caller, are dropped in batch 6's flattening rung (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the three `Number`-typed big operators). The judgement's library slips are ledger rows 421-423 (row 423 closing with the drop).

The launch advice that messages are safe was right; this entry's headline, "his message interrupted a turn" and "a message is safe only while the coordinator is idle" are wrong (session `fe616d40`, main transcript 12:07:33-12:10:46 and 16:13:08; `subagents/workflows/wf_eb47c103-304/`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The container -->
- **A manual compaction issued between turns leaves a running Workflow alive** (found 2026-09-19 by a worker in the archived transcript of session `bdff267d`, `transcripts` branch, parts file `001.jsonl`): the eight-rung climb's run `wf_73833dfb-d25` (launched 2026-09-17 06:00:57 UTC) survived two `/compact` commands, boundaries 10:47:33 (442,504 tokens before, 130 s) and 14:25:25 (177,831 tokens, 153 s), both typed while the session sat between turns; rung 5's commit landed 84 s after the first boundary, rungs 6-8 and the final re-run followed, and the run's completion notification arrived 14:39:09 with all eight rungs. This container's three compactions (09-18 18:38, 22:54; 09-19 06:38) coincided with no run. So the rule is: compact between turns, never send during a turn; the 09-19 death was a mid-turn interrupt, not a compaction. Caveat: that run's journal and agent transcripts are not in the backup, so the agents' survival is inferred from their commits and the session's own status turns. Corrected 2026-09-26: "never send during a turn" is wrong, since a message sent during a turn is queued and kills nothing (the entry above, corrected); and the caveat is closed: three manual compactions in this container fell inside live runs, 09-19 09:47 (`wf_3b5a273c-a80`), 09-20 05:32 (`wf_d1628adb-2ee`) and 09-26 12:26 (`wf_88172730-ebe`), and each run's agents kept writing through the compaction (40 to 66 records inside its window) and went on to their results (session `fe616d40`, `subagents/workflows/`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The container -->
- **Stopping a turn kills every background agent alive at that moment; a message sent while the coordinator is busy kills nothing** (2026-09-26, `coordinator/interrupt-archaeology/judgement.md` § 1, from `coordinator/interrupt-archaeology/evidence.md`; session `fe616d40`, main transcript, `subagents/` and `subagents/workflows/`; session `bdff267d`, `transcripts` branch, `001.jsonl`). The kill is the turn interrupt the transcript records as "[Request interrupted by user]", with any tool still in flight recorded "User rejected tool use": in the four interrupts that met live background agents (2026-09-19 07:46:42, 09-22 07:18:51, 09-25 22:31:59, 09-26 12:07:47) all seven agents alive died at that instant, Workflow agents and `Agent`-tool workers alike, and none ever survived one. Eleven messages and three `/context` commands sent while the coordinator was busy, during five live runs from 09-19 to 09-26, killed nothing: each was queued and delivered inside the running turn or as the next turn. Five manual compactions between turns killed nothing either (09-17 10:47 and 14:25, 09-19 09:47, 09-20 05:32, 09-26 12:26). That the stop button sent the interrupt is confirmed for 09-25 in Pavol's words and very likely for 09-26 (the iOS client's stop control under his right thumb), not shown for 09-19; the transcripts record the effect, not the control. Not tested: an automatic compaction mid-turn, and an interrupt during the Stop hook while a run is alive. The rule: send messages at any time; compact between turns; do not stop a turn while the session is working, including the seconds after a reply while the transcript backup runs; after an accidental stop, say so and the batch is relaunched (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the interrupt ruling). The three entries above carry the corrections.

### The checker and the one library

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: re-measured on the flat library, where walk refuses a `ZZ32` into `Box[\RR64\]` as it refuses `Wide`/`Narrow` (`reviews/numerics-plan-fable.md` § 3.1), the scalar operators' lines re-anchored after climb batch 6 moved them, and a numeral's reach pointed to -->
- **An inferred generic refuses a coercion that the method it forwards to accepts, on both paths** (2026-09-26, `reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review/row388-container-probe.md`, programs and captures beside it; Astra's prediction in `reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review.md` § 3; ledger row 388 extended). With an invariant `Box[\T\]`, `b: Box[\Wide\]` and `n: Narrow`, where `Wide` declares `coerce` from `Narrow`: `b.accept(n)` and `acceptBox[\Wide\](b, n)` convert on both paths. The inferred `acceptBox(b, n)` is refused: walk infers `T` as `Object`, then reports a unification error, and the compiled checker says "not applicable". The top-level operator `b n` is refused on both. An operator declared inside `Box` converts compiled and is refused under walk. With `Box[\RR64\]` and a `ZZ32` argument, walk accepts all four by today's subtyping and returns the integer 3, not 3.0, while the compiled path, which has no `ZZ32`-to-`RR64` coercion, refuses all four. `RR32` into `Box[\RR64\]` compiled splits as `Wide`/`Narrow` does. So after the flattening, the library's top-level `Matrix`-scalar operators (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2631-2660`) would refuse a narrower scalar that `scale` accepts, unless row 388 is fixed or the operators are declared inside the traits.

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: the mixed-width answer measured against the one library, which the note had not reached (`reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` §§ 3.2, 4.2, 7.1), and row 146's closing folded in -->
- **The flattening's three questions, measured by a clean worker** (2026-09-26, `reviews/flattening-questions-ways.md`, about 30 probes and captures under `reviews/flattening-questions-ways/`). *The empty sum.* The interpreter's empty sum is `0 : Int` for every element type. A one-reduction-per-element-type design reached from one generic declaration is the library's own pattern (`BitXor`, `MINNUM`, `CompilerLibrary`'s `ZZ32Addition`, the specification's `SumZZ32`). But a no-argument form cannot be overloaded by result type alone (measured), and the library's way around it, a static parameter plus a `typecase` over a `() -> T` witness, works under walk and is rejected by the compiled checker as written. C4 needs a `ZZ32` zero for `matOffset(0)` (`run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:43`), `RR64` results for `SUM e`, `SUM vm` and `DOT`, and `RR64`'s own `MAX`. *Mixed widths.* Under walk a variable declared `ZZ64` that holds a literal does 32-bit arithmetic (`a + b = -2147483648`, the defect in the exclusion fork's entry above), and a range from 2^31-1 to a `ZZ64` enumerates wrapped `Int`s. The compiled checker infers a union for a generic call over mixed widths, which crashed code generation. The two programs have no `ZZ64` variables, but they need `ZZ32`-to-`RR64` and literal-to-`RR64` coercions, which the compiled prelude lacks. *`RationalQuantity`.* The compiled checker rejects it ("Cyclic type hierarchy") and walk cannot instantiate it. The library never had it or any sign-refined type. *History, correcting the record's attribution:* the compiler prelude's tower was not flattened by Steele in 2011. David Chase cut the subtyping on 2009-08-31 (`6896886fb`), Sukyoung Ryu added the exclusions (`3e0306166`, 2009-10-16), the coercions came in 2009-2010, and Steele built the operators on the flat prelude later (the note's Question 1 § 7). POSITIONS 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 carry the earlier attribution in the record's words at the time.

<!-- moved 2026-09-27 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: `RangeInternals`' new sites and the natives' errors given their causes by the triage, `ExtentScalarRange`'s crash seen again under ranges over `ZZ32` (measure C), and the `any` setting and the unchanged library measured three times more -->
- **The true distance to the switch-over, measured on today's tree: on the flat library the checker reports 1,736 distinct errors under walk's setting and 1,527 under the compile path's, of which the gate's count shows 62** (2026-09-27, answer 11's measurement, `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat.md`, scripts and captures under `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/`, on the sources of `d65892d34`; on the nested tower of 2026-09-26 the totals were 2,523 and 2,359, `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance.md`). Over twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, the overloading memo off, under walk's setting and the compile path's own `extends Object` setting respectively: exclusion 38 and 38; `comprises` 2 and 2; overloading 501 and 251; return type 91 and 85; abstract method not implemented 18 and 30; the `extends Object` bound 0 and 372; other well-formedness 93 and 93; component bodies' type errors 981 and 645; export mismatches 12 and 11. The flattening removed 505 return-type sites, 169 same-parameter overloading pairs and 88 exclusion sites; 167 new body-error sites appeared, 113 of them in `RangeInternals`, where generic code compares a type-parameter integral with a literal (that they passed through `Number`'s catch-alls before is inferred, not traced); batch 6's 21 new native bindings show as errors under walk's setting. ### The checker and the one library

<!-- moved 2026-09-28 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: rung H's clearing of the flat library's 18 exclusion errors, appended by the gather, folded in as the present, with the gate's count of exclusion errors as its source -->
- **The compiled checker's exclusion rule is the designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion", relaxing it alone is unsound, and the real fork is the code generator's dispatch of generics** (2026-09-22: rung P of batch 3 stopped, `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-relax/REPORT.md`, taken into the tree at the batch's gather; `reviews/multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md`; `reviews/mie-probes/dispatch-and-route-c.md`). The rule "forbids multiple instantiation inheritance, in which a type is a subtype of distinct applications of a type constructor" (`Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152`; Naden 2012, `Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497`, who records that it conflicts with the numeric tower and leaves that open, `:568-632`); it entered the checker 2010-05-28 (`5a6b7913b`) and became `checkP` 2010-07-26 (`e828b44b1`); the nested tower is 2008. The compiled checker enforces it in the two hierarchy questions and relies on it in the return-type rule (`OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105`); with it relaxed under any placement, `ProbeMIEPick.fss` type-checks and dies with `IncompatibleClassChangeError`. The interpreter has no such clause, dispatches a generic on a double-member object by the first-listed instantiation (`FType.java:568-574`), refuses overloads lacking an excluding pair, and dies at run time on other shapes. Pavol chose route A, keep the rule and flatten the tower (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, the exclusion route, rung P's fork), and it is built: the interpreter converts by coercion (climb batch 4 rung C), the specification states the rule (climb batch 5 rung S) and the number tower is flat (climb batch 6 rung F). The routes not taken were dropping the rule (22 lines, 93 → 33 then, with the dispatcher changed to take the call site's static arguments, since sized at 43 lines in "The exclusion fork, priced three ways and dated" below) and a per-trait guard (28 lines, refusing 69 library pairs, the tower's own implementations). On the nested tower the rule bit 61 errors at 23 library declarations (13 tower, 4 comparisons, 4 `Maybe`, 2 reductions); on the flat library the count stage shows 18 exclusion errors, at the comparison and `Maybe` families and at `RelationalPredicateCondition` ("The true distance to the switch-over" below). Climb batch 7's rung H (`952892a00`) cleared those 18 (`compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/REPORT.md` sections 4 to 9): `TotalComparison` extends `Comparison` alone, as the compiler prelude's does (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:719-722`), and extends no order, as the specification's does, whose supertypes are `Comparison` and the three traits of `LEXICO`'s algebra (`Specification/advanced-lib/comparison.tex:28-32`), restating `>=`, `<=`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX` at itself with `StandardTotalOrder`'s bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:170-175`); `AnyMaybe` extends `AnyUniqueItem` alone and writes the `opr =` its api declares (`.fss:1400-1403`); `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` no longer excludes its own supertype, its component-only second `ANDCOND` renamed `andRelCond` and chosen by a `typecase` in `andCondCombine` at `FilterGenerator2`'s two call sites (`.fss:4514`, `:4516`, `:4556-4566`), zero.md's P3d with the two changes the compiled checker needs. The cost: a program's own `p1 ANDCOND p2` of two relational predicates is no longer relational under walk, while `filter` keeps the fusion (row 458). On the flat library the checker now reports no exclusion error (`compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/probes/distance-postedit.txt:3`). Dispatch, measured: a static argument is a constant in the loaded class's name only when no dispatch is needed; a dispatched generic arm reads it from the run-time value, which records only its last-listed instantiation (`OverloadSet.java:1411-1696`, `STypesUtil.scala:1276`). `MieDispatchSub` (generic overloads on `Tag[\X\]` and on its subtrait `Sub[\X\]`, called with an object that extends `Sub[\Red\]` and `Tag[\Blue\]` and so is a double member of `Tag`) is refused by today's checker with four hierarchy errors (`reviews/mie-probes/MieDispatchSub.compiled.txt:1-11`); with the rule relaxed it compiles and throws `ClassCastException` (`:12-18`). Two defects need no double membership: a generic arm reached through a less specific declaration throws whenever its return type mentions its parameter (`reviews/mie-probes/scope/ScopeAlpha2.compiled.txt:1-6`), and a run-time-made `ZZ32` instantiation is named differently from the static one (`scope/ScopeZZ32Sub.compiled.txt:1-6`); both programs are legal under route A, type-check on today's checker and die with `ClassCastException`, and the 43-line call-site change fixes both inside template dispatchers only (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md` § 4). And the overloading checker never examines symbolic operators (`OverloadingChecker.scala:546-550`). None of the three has a ledger row (`reviews/batch-3-conformance.md`, rung P).

- **The exclusion fork, priced three ways and dated** (2026-09-23, five notes under `reviews/mie-probes/`). On these prices Pavol chose to keep the rule, route A (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, the exclusion route, rung P's fork). *Dated* (`spec-sentences-dated.md`): the spec's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters is 2009 text (Sukyoung Ryu, before the rule entered the checker in 2010) never revised; the passages allowing double membership are 2008-2009 text untouched through 2012; only the advanced chapter's meet-rule preamble was rewritten in 2010, author lost; `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is not a genuine 2008 snapshot for three of these files. *Keep the rule* (`price-keep-the-rule.md`, `keep/`): 14 declaration headers flattened the compiler prelude's way (`Number` loses its algebra and 52 catch-alls, `RR64` takes the algebra on); 367 sites certainly need a conversion (160 library, 207 in 35 test files; microGPT 37 through `Number`'s catch-alls), measured by an observing shadow over all 392 interpreter tests; the interpreter needs coercion called at dispatch (`OverloadedFunction.bestMatch`'s "TODO add checks for COERCE", about 150-200 lines in six files, run-time choice where the spec's is static; built by climb batch 4 rung C); count 103 → 22; and a defect found on the way: `x: ZZ64 = 2147483647; x + 1` printed the wrapped negative because the value stayed 32-bit (row 146, closed by climb batch 6 rung F). *Drop the rule* (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md`, `scope/`): the dispatcher is already loaded under the call site's static arguments and only its arms read the value; making the arms use the dispatcher's own arguments is 43 lines in `OverloadSet.java`, `MieDispatchSub`, which today's checker refuses as a double member of `Tag`, then compiles with the rule relaxed and answers `Marker[Blue]`, the compiler prelude byte-identical, all 43 generic-overload compiler tests print the same; not built for dotted and functional methods, `opr`/`nat`; the spec's overload sentence enforced refuses 179 library api pairs under the narrow reading (11 errors already) and 335 under the wide one, which refuses the tower's own method implementations; padding a family to one parameter list passes on both paths; 6 compiler and 6 interpreter tests refused; symbolic operators, never examined by the checker, add 329 pairs; the spec also says (`overloading.tex:173-175`) static parameters are inferred before applicability for dynamic calls, citing an empty chapter. *Literature* (`literature.md`): the Fortress group kept the rule after 2012 (Welterweight 2012, POPL 2019, which checks the return type at run time); Java, Kotlin, Scala, X10 keep it with flat numbers; C#, F#, Rust, Haskell allow double membership and choose statically; Julia avoids it by single inheritance and gives up static soundness; nobody published a resolution under run-time dispatch nor a proof the rule is necessary. *The 2012 patents' forest rule* (`patents-forest-rule.md`, `forest/`; US 8,843,887 col. 8 l. 8-12, US 8,898,632 col. 8 l. 23-27, Chase, Steele, Naden, Hilburn, Luchangco, filed 2012-08-31): a self-typed generic (one that "comprises exactly T") may be carried at several instantiations if they form a chain; in a shadow `checkP` accepting the library's F-bound as the test it lifts 48 of the 61 (tower 31, comparisons 7, `Maybe` 10; the reductions' 13 stay, `DistributesOver` is not self-typed), count 103 → 37 against 24 with the rule dropped; under the patents' literal `comprises T` test nothing is lifted, no library trait has the clause (`CompilerAlgebra.fsi:16, :24` do); it does not close the specialisation hole (a specialisation at `Mid` catches `Narrow` values; calls typed `Eq[Narrow]` die with `IncompatibleClassChangeError`), which needs a covariant reading, dispatch agreeing with it, a return-type rule over every level below a specialisation (40-70 lines, derived, not in the patents), the call-site fix, and seven library declarations completed; Welterweight's `static.tick:83-89` states the blanket rule and its self-typed dispatch step is commented out. The keep-the-rule count 103 → 22 was measured on a library copy before climb batch 4, whose rung N added 22 `Invalid overloading of fill` errors that the flattening does not remove (the count 103 → 125); the flat library as landed by climb batch 6 rung F reads 62 ("The true distance to the switch-over" below).

- **The compiled checker does not enforce the specification's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters; forced past the api's early return, its overloading check reports 482 errors on the one library, and four defects sit on the way** (2026-09-26, `reviews/overload-static-params-ways.md` §§ 2-3, a clean worker; 25 two-path probes and captures under `reviews/overload-static-params-ways/`). The checker applies the Types paper's rules and refuses only pairs it cannot prove: open traits, and `CAP`, whose domains exclude only through the exclusion rule plus a bound, a step it lacks. Forced past the `FortressLibrary` api's early return (a guarded copy of `StaticChecker.java`), the overloading check reports 482 errors: 421 in `FortressLibrary`, 39 in `RangeInternals`, 22 in `NativeArray`. By the two arms' static parameters: different lists 29; one generic and one plain 137; same list 58; both plain 215; duplicates 43. All 132 generic-plus-plain return-type errors and the 43 duplicates have a plain arm on a tower or `Comparison` type that the checker reports as excluding its own supertypes (`FortressLibrary.fsi:121`, `:373`, `:438`, `:465`); the worker reads these as artefacts the flattening removes, not re-run on a flat library. The four defects: walk's choice between a generic and a plain arm depends on declaration order (`OverloadedFunction.java:871-892`); the return-type rule checks one solved instance where the paper asks for all (`OverloadingOracle.scala:81-117`), so the paper's own counterexample passes and fails the JVM verifier and a permuted override throws `ClassCastException` (row 398); code generation fails for two generic arms on a bare type variable; walk runs an arm whose static parameter is in no parameter type with that parameter unbound, while the compiled path never chooses it (row 400). Also a declaration slip: `StandardMinMax` declares `MIN` returning `(T,T)` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:209-210`) where the body returns one `T` (`FortressLibrary.fss:260-261`). The sentence dates from 2009-10; the 1.0 release of 2008 compared generic arms by their bounds; the later restart's overloading chapter omits the sentence. The slip is ledger row 421 (2026-09-26).

ℤ, ℤ64, ℤ32, ℕ64, ℕ32, ℚ and ℝ64 are siblings under `Number`, each a subtype of `Number` and none of another, with rung F's coercions: ℚ from the five integer types, ℝ64 from ℤ32 and integer numerals (answer 8's words), ℤ64 from ℤ32 and ℕ32, ℕ64 from ℕ32, ℤ from the four fixed widths, every other conversion explicit, the one into ℝ64 written `asFloat(x)` with the method the one library declares on `Number` (named at the gather, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:284`) (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-49`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:16-37`). 367 sites certainly need a conversion (160 library, 207 in 35 test files; microGPT 37 through `Number`'s catch-alls), measured by an observing shadow over all 392 interpreter tests; the interpreter needs coercion called at dispatch (`OverloadedFunction.bestMatch`'s "TODO add checks for COERCE", about 150-200 lines in six files, run-time choice where the spec's is static; built by climb batch 4 rung C); count 103 → 22; and a defect found on the way: `x: ZZ64 = 2147483647; x + 1` printed the wrapped negative because the value stayed 32-bit (row 146, closed by climb batch 6 rung F). *Drop the rule* (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md`, `scope/`): the dispatcher is already loaded under the call site's static arguments and only its arms read the value; Java, Kotlin, Scala, X10 keep it with flat numbers; C#, F#, Rust, Haskell allow double membership and choose statically; Julia avoids it by single inheritance and gives up static soundness; nobody published a resolution under run-time dispatch nor a proof the rule is necessary. *The 2012 patents' forest rule* (`patents-forest-rule.md`, `forest/`; US 8,843,887 col. 8 l. 8-12, US 8,898,632 col. 8 l. 23-27, Chase, Steele, Naden, Hilburn, Luchangco, filed 2012-08-31): a self-typed generic (one that "comprises exactly T") may be carried at several instantiations if they form a chain; - The interpreter's integer rules: fixed-width `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `|..|`, `DIV` and multiplication raise a catchable `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit (climb batch 6b's rung O, `917bb7b32`; "Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" below); `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` and `NN64` saturate at the width and reverse on a negative count, the count read by the class of its value (an `NN64` count of `2^63` or more is beyond the width, a `ZZ` count is read exactly); the unbounded `ZZ`'s shift count is exact at any size, a negative one giving `0` or `-1` and an unrepresentable left shift a catchable `IntegerOverflow`, refused before the JVM allocates it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/BigNum.java:247`); `GCD` and `LCM` on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` are nonnegative and an unrepresentable result, `MIN GCD 0` and `MIN GCD MIN` included, is a catchable `IntegerOverflow`; `LCM` on the unbounded `ZZ` is nonnegative (`BigNum.java:176-192`); `0 LCM 0` is `0` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ`, and on `NN32` and `NN64` since the review's repair (row 385); `ZZ64.narrow` keeps the low 32 bits; the specification's `shift` is declared on `ZZ` (next entry) and absent from the compiler prelude (row 383, expected failure `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXShiftDeclRungI.test`). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. Since rung K of climb batch 4 (`57600bc27`), a `ZZ32` receiver shifted by a count of any integral type is answered by `ZZ32`'s own method at width 32 and is a `ZZ32` (`3 LSHIFT big(widen(33))` is `0 : ZZ32`, and so for `NN32` and `NN64` counts and for `RSHIFT`), because `ZZ32`'s pair is declared `opr LSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):ZZ32` and `opr RSHIFT(self,b:AnyIntegral):ZZ32` in both files (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:688-691`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:491-492`), as `Integral[\I\]` promises (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:431-432`), on Pavol's decision of 2026-09-24 (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, ledger rows 380 and 381), which lifted batch 3.5's reservation for these four declarations only; `ZZ64`'s api pair now matches its component (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:530-531`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:756-759`), so no integer trait of the interpreter's library declares an operator of `Integral` with a parameter type other than the one `Integral` promises (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-shift-count/probes/integral-contract.txt`). The api edits change nothing `walk` runs, since `walk` dispatches on the component, and nothing the checker-count stage reports, since the `FortressLibrary` api stops at its hierarchy errors (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java:219`, `:269-272`) before the overloading checker (`:274-275`): 103 before and after, measured on its branch from `47437c65f`, without rung N, the full checker output byte-identical (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-shift-count/probes/checker-count-before.txt`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-shift-count/probes/checker-count-after.txt`). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss:89`, which compares value and type through its helper `zz32Shown` (`:14-18`) (`d6faad28f`, `c9faa7df4`, `57600bc27`; `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, `compile-ladder/rung-shift-count/REPORT.md`).
