### The container

<!-- moved 2026-09-28 from FACTS.md § The container: the resume's longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls in call order folded in, from the stop of 2026-09-28 at 20:34:04 UTC and the resume of batch 6.5's first run, wf_fa14416d-889 -->
- **A restart of the session's own process kills its background runs, and `resumeFromRunId` then recovers every agent that had finished** (2026-09-27, session `fe616d40`). At 12:09:17 UTC the environment manager restarted the session's Claude Code process (`environment-manager task-run … --session-mode resume`; the VM itself was not restarted, `uptime -s` still 2026-09-26 23:11:31, kernel fc-v37); the cause is not visible from inside. Batch 6b's run `wf_08949b8a-a21` and an `Agent`-tool worker died with it: the run's repair agent's transcript ends 12:09, four minutes into its stage. The conversation, worktrees, untracked files and transcripts survived. A relaunch from the base (12:12, `wf_2da3e152-2d5`) restarted at the first stage; the same script and arguments with `resumeFromRunId: wf_08949b8a-a21` (12:20) took rung O's worker, skeptic and judge from the old run's `journal.jsonl` without running them (the journal keys match when the script text and arguments are identical) and started the repair stage anew. So after a death that leaves the session, its ID and the run's journal in place, the run is resumed with the same script text, not relaunched; a finished agent's result is kept, an unfinished one runs from its start, and its worktree's leftovers are its starting point. A run whose script has changed since launch is resumed from a copy of the script as launched (`git show <base>:<path>`). What does not carry over is a new session: `remote-container.md` § The 2026-09-18 restart and step 5 of the recovery list. The same restart undid a compaction: the resumed process rebuilt the conversation from the transcript as if the manual compaction of 08:40 had not happened, from the one of 03:28 on, so the context the model saw went from 421K on the last call before the restart to 802K on the first after it with nothing new in the chat, and the automatic compaction fired at 12:11 at 805K. Measured: the 12:11 boundary's `cumulativeDroppedTokens`, 8,783,976, is the 03:28 boundary's 7,994,881 plus its own 789,095, leaving out the 08:40 compaction's 741,537, and the 03:28 boundary record appears a second time in the transcript at the reload (lines 25826 and 32220); what the reload sent beyond that is inferred, not shown (`explorations/reviews/coordinator-context-2026-09-27.md`, `e15e1a01a`). After a restart of the session's process, `/context` shows whether it happened again. It happened again on 2026-09-28: the session's process started anew at 07:36:42 UTC, the VM not restarted (`uptime -s` still 2026-09-27 18:39:21). Batch 7R's run, three `Agent`-tool workers and the push loop stopped, while shell scripts the workers had started in the background kept running (probe K's `run-all.sh`, started 05:51, and a comparison pass of rung J's). The run was resumed at 07:38 with the same script and arguments and `resumeFromRunId`: rung U's worker and skeptic came from the journal, and rung J's worker started anew under the same key. The `Agent`-tool workers continued from their transcripts on a `SendMessage`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-28 from FACTS.md § The container: the stop of 2026-09-28 at 20:34:04 UTC added, the stops counted to 136, and the four runs' length, given as 46,656 s give or take a second, corrected to the log's 46,636 to 46,660 s over the five -->
- **The platform stops the session's process after about 12 hours 58 minutes of continuous running, and restarts it in resume mode within seconds** (2026-09-28, the environment manager's log `/tmp/env-manager.log`, read by the coordinator). Every stop in the log is a `SIGTERM` from outside ("Received signal, shutting down gracefully", signal `terminated`, 135 since 2026-09-08), followed by "Claude Code stopped due to context cancellation" with the run's length, then "Set session mode for environment" `resume`. Four runs ended at the same length, 46,656 s give or take a second: 2026-09-20 03:45:13, 09-26 22:02:00, 09-27 12:09:17 and 09-28 07:36:42 UTC; the rest are short runs of a few minutes to a few hours that end when the session goes idle. So the restarts of 09-27 12:09 and 09-28 07:36 ("A restart of the session's own process ..." above) were this cap, not a crash, not memory and not a message; they fall while Pavol is talking because the process runs continuously only while he or a check-in keeps it busy. Any restart, a VM start included, resets the clock, so the next stop is predictable: the last start plus 12 h 58 min. A check-in armed a few minutes after that time resumes what the stop killed.

- **The flattening's three questions, measured by a clean worker** (2026-09-26, `reviews/flattening-questions-ways.md`, about 30 probes and captures under `reviews/flattening-questions-ways/`). *The empty sum.* The interpreter's empty sum is `0 : Int` for every element type. A one-reduction-per-element-type design reached from one generic declaration is the library's own pattern (`BitXor`, `MINNUM`, `CompilerLibrary`'s `ZZ32Addition`, the specification's `SumZZ32`). But a no-argument form cannot be overloaded by result type alone (measured), and the library's way around it, a static parameter plus a `typecase` over a `() -> T` witness, works under walk and is rejected by the compiled checker as written. C4 needs a `ZZ32` zero for `matOffset(0)` (`run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:43`), `RR64` results for `SUM e`, `SUM vm` and `DOT`, and `RR64`'s own `MAX`. *Mixed widths.* On the nested tower, under walk a variable declared `ZZ64` that held a literal did 32-bit arithmetic (`a + b = -2147483648`, the defect in the exclusion fork's entry above, row 146, closed by climb batch 6 rung F), and a range from 2^31-1 to a `ZZ64` enumerated wrapped `Int`s. The compiled checker with its own prelude infers a union for a generic call over mixed widths, which crashed code generation. The note did not reach the checker over the one library; measured there since, on the flat library, the checker infers a union and walk a common supertype, and neither converts ("Static arguments are inferred from the arguments alone, on both paths, and never through a coercion" below). The two programs have no `ZZ64` variables, but they need `ZZ32`-to-`RR64` and literal-to-`RR64` coercions, which the compiled prelude lacks and the one library has: the programs' `1.0 s` and `1 - beta1` shapes are `RR64` on both paths against it (`reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` § 7.1). *`RationalQuantity`.* The compiled checker rejects it ("Cyclic type hierarchy") and walk cannot instantiate it. The library never had it or any sign-refined type. *History, correcting the record's attribution:* the compiler prelude's tower was not flattened by Steele in 2011. David Chase cut the subtyping on 2009-08-31 (`6896886fb`), Sukyoung Ryu added the exclusions (`3e0306166`, 2009-10-16), the coercions came in 2009-2010, and Steele built the operators on the flat prelude later (the note's Question 1 § 7). POSITIONS 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 carry the earlier attribution in the record's words at the time.

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: rewritten to state the present after climb batch N's rungs I and K: both paths infer a generic call's static arguments with coercion and answer 8's promotion, and the checker keeps the expected type at `f(x)`; the two appended sentences folded in; the base's mechanism and its refusals, superseded, kept here; the title, now false, kept, since entries are cited by it -->
- **Static arguments are inferred from the arguments alone, on both paths, and never through a coercion** (2026-09-27, `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` §§ 3-4 and 8, probes and captures under `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/probes-B/`: the compiled checker against the one library by `check.sh`, walk by `walk.sh`, private caches). The checker's constraint is "argType <: domain", with "range <: context" added when a context is given (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:928-947`); its solver binds each variable to the join of its lower bounds, a union (`scala_src/typechecker/Formula.scala:527`, `scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:80-81`), with one heuristic, a single lower bound's ancestors (`Formula.scala:528-541`); `checkApplicableWithInference` is "with static argument inference and no coercion" (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:171-173`), and the coercion oracle targets only trait, tuple and arrow types (`scala_src/typechecker/CoercionOracle.scala:92`, `:145-155`). Walk unifies each argument's run-time type with its declared parameter type, whatever that type mentions, before any conversion (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/EvaluatorBase.java:131-181`), joins two lower bounds to their least common supertype (`evaluator/types/FType.java:350-380`), and rung C's coercion pass skips every generic arm (`evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:826`). The specification says "types named by type parameters *do not have coercions*" (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:363-365`) and nothing more on the point ("The specification never wrote static-argument inference, a numeral's type hierarchy or a range's integer width" under The specification and the repository's lineage). Measured: a numeral or a `ZZ32` for a declared `ZZ64` or `RR64` parameter of a generic function whose static argument is inferred (`scale64(BoxT[\String\](2), 3)`, `scaleR`) is refused on both paths and converted with the static argument written, row 388's shape reached by a numeral; a mixed-width call gets a union on the checker (`pick(l, 3)` with `l: ZZ64` is `OR(ZZ64,IntLiteral)`, and `l#3` was a `CompactFullRange[\OR(ZZ64,IntLiteral)\]` while the range operators were generic, before climb batch 7R's rung J put them over `ZZ32` alone) and `AnyIntegral` under walk, and an `Integral[\T\]` F-bound refuses it on both (`twice(l, 3)`, `twice(l, z)`); the ancestor heuristic makes `inc(5)` a `ZZ32`; a non-generic operator promotes by coercion resolution, `u + 1` with `u: NN32` a `ZZ64` on both paths; a numeral in a body generic over `Integral[\T\]` (`x + 1`) is refused by the checker and runs under walk, where `inc(u)` for `u: NN32` returns `6 : Long` from a function declared to return `T` (row 387). A parameter nothing fixes becomes `BottomType` on the checker when it has a bound (`mkB[\T extends Integral[\T\]\]()` is `BoxT[\BottomType\]`) and "Could not infer static argument T without context" when it has none, because under the bound `Any` the whole constraint is trivially true and the variable is left open (`Formula.scala:493`; `measure-D.md` § 2.1); the compile path gives every empty `extends` clause `Object` (row 412) and so takes the `Bottom` branch (rows 425, 447); walk erases to `BOTTOM` (`EvaluatorBase.java:245`, row 424). The expected type: the checker passes it at a typed binding, a declared return type, a block's last expression and the branches of an `if … else`, and keeps it at a method invocation and an operator (`a: BoxT[\ZZ64\] = Fac.mk()` is accepted with `T = ZZ64`, and under that binding `Fac.wrap(3)`, `BOXOF 3` and `3 OPLUS 4` are refused), but drops it at a call written `f(x)` (row 455; the next entry). Walk has no static context: a typed binding converts after the call (`a: ZZ64 = idt(3)` is `3 : Long`). Since climb batch N's rung I (`8dc1a74d9`) this holds for walk only until rung K. The compiled checker infers with coercion and answer 8's promotion and keeps the expected type at `f(x)` (the entry "The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion ..."): `pick(l, 3)` is a `ZZ64` there, and `scale64(BoxT[\String\](2), 3)` checks. Walk's half is superseded by climb batch N's rung K (`041682188`; "Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion ..." under Landed semantics): `scale64(BoxT[\String\](2), 3)` and `scale64(…, z)` run with the argument converted, `twice(l, z)` is `ZZ64`, a mixed-width call takes the narrowest type its arguments convert into, and walk still has no static context, so a typed binding converts a call's result after the call and cannot fix a static argument that only the result mentions (row 510).

- **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion and answer 8's promotion, keeps the expected type at a call written `f(x)`, ranks every declaration applicable only with coercion together, generic or not, and refuses a tie among them unless it is a numeral's** (2026-09-29, climb batch N rung I, `8dc1a74d9`; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md`). **The attempts.** A call's candidates are tried by subtyping with the expected type; failing that with coercion; failing that both again without it. The first attempt is by subtyping under the expected type and counts only candidates without a coercion the call needs; a declaration that fits the call's arguments but whose result the expected type refuses is not among its candidates. So when none fits under the expected type, the attempt with coercion ranks every declaration applicable with coercion (the coercion chapter's Σ′), and a declaration reached by coercion whose result fits can win over one that fits the arguments as they are: `a: V = k(NOf(1))`, with `k[\T extends N\](x: T): T` beside `k(x: V): V` and `V` coercing from `N`, runs `k(V)`, where the base and walk run the generic. That is new at a call written `f(x)` and the base's behaviour at a method invocation, the reserved stop "a ranking that lets a declaration needing a conversion win over one that fits the call as it is", met and listed (row 508, gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXInferContextKeepsFit`). An attempt is kept only when its most specific candidate's result converts to the expected type. A call no attempt keeps takes the first attempt holding a candidate: for a call written `f(x)`, among the attempts without the context, so that the binding reports a call the rule accepts; for any other call, among those with it, which keeps today's message (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:604-752`; `Operators.scala:85`, `:90`, `:197`, `:345`). **The coercion attempt** (`checkApplicableWithCoercion`, `Functionals.scala:280-400`). A type parameter that is a position's whole type takes the narrowest type, under the coercion chapter's no-less-specific relation, among its arguments' types, the types they coerce to and its bound. The types they coerce to come from a new lookup from a source to its coercion targets (`CoercionOracle.getCoercionTargetsFrom`, over `TraitTable.coercingTraits`). Structured positions and the expected type constrain the solver by subtyping. Every argument is then admitted by subtyping or coercion. It refuses a call with an untyped function argument and one with more than 64 combinations of chosen types (rows 507 and 506). **The promotion.** A candidate that subtyping instantiates with a union is instantiated again at the narrowest named type (`pick(z, l)`: `ZZ64`, `z` converted). **The ranking.** A candidate with a counted coercion ranks below one without; a promoted candidate's coercions are not counted. A promoted candidate, and a generic one of the coercion attempt, are compared on their declared domains by the overloading oracle's subtyping, strictly one way; between two converted candidates it decides when it relates them one way, and the coercion chapter's order on the instances decides otherwise (`useful/STypesUtil.scala:1064-1113`; `CoercionOracle.scala:76-84`). **The head and the tie.** The head is the specification's maximal element. A tie among candidates with counted coercions is refused, "Ambiguous coercion in call to function f: ...", a generic declaration listed by its declared domain. The exception is a tie differing only where the argument is a numeral: the numeral is read as `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by a literal's magnitude (a size used as a value as `ZZ32`), and the call resolves as an argument of that type would, over every candidate, those the reading fits without coercion first (`pickb(3000000000)` beside `pickb(NN32)`, `pickb(ZZ32)` and `pickb(ZZ64)` takes `pickb(ZZ64)`). A numeral too large for every declaration is refused. An unconverted tie keeps today's head. **Measured on the compiler tests.** Against the base, 4 of the 415 `.fss` files the gate's compiler tests then compiled or linked change their diagnostics, 493 errors to 483: rows 401 and 388's expected failures now check, and are promoted to `NatLitArgChecker` and `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC`. The ambiguity check refuses no call there but its two tests' own (`XXXInferAmbiguousCoercion`, `XXXInferSigmaTie`), and `XXX6bu`'s pinned message is kept. **The count and the distance.** The checker count (75) and the distance (626) are site for site the landed gate's. The ladder's 85 files and their 170 outputs are unchanged. **The judgement's programs, compiled.** `OpAnyZW`'s `op(z, w)` runs the generic at `ZZ64`; `O2Z64`'s runs `plain64`; `O2Num`'s `op(1, w)` runs the generic at `ZZ64`; `O2Meet`, `O2Pos` and `O2Tie` are unchanged. `g(NOf(1), 5)` with `g[\T\](x: W1, y: T)` beside `g(x: W2, y: Any)`, both reached only by coercion, runs the generic. **`ZZ32` with `NN32`** gives `ZZ` under the compiler library, whose `ZZ64` declares no coercion from `NN32` (row 442), gated as the expected failure `XXXInferPromoteNN32`; `ZZ64` under the one library. **On the numeral switch's library copy.** The shadow's probe program goes from 29 error sites to 4, and Q1's cases are taken (`lohi(2, 46)` and `twice(3, 4)` at `ZZ32`; `widen(4)` and `pickn(3)` at `ZZ32`'s declarations; `OneShapeW` 36 sites to 5). The library's two numeral strides are taken at `:`. `z CMP 0` is refused as ambiguous: row 484's shape through `StandardTotalOrder`'s inherited `CMP`. **Not reached.** A result-only parameter is still bound to `BottomType`, and now under the bound `Any` too when an expected type is at `f(x)`, where it was refused; such a call compiles and fails JVM verification at load. - **The one library's number tower is flat** (2026-09-27, climb batch 6 rung F, `d846e3644`; `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/`; rows 146, 423, 428). `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ` and `RR64` are siblings under `Number` (`Number comprises { RR64, QQ, AnyIntegral }`, `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32 }`), each carrying its own algebra: `RR64` and `QQ` extend `StandardPartialOrder`, `StandardMinMax`, `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing` at their own type, and `Integral[\I\]` extends `StandardTotalOrder[\I\]`, `MultiplicativeRing[\I\]` and `AnyIntegral` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:281-611`; `NN32` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi`). - **Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion, answer 8's promotion is walk's number case, and the declaration an overloaded call chooses is re-instantiated by it** (2026-09-29, climb batch N rung K, `041682188`; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md`). `EvaluatorBase.inferAndInstantiateGenericFunction` unifies, as before, only the arguments whose declared type mentions a static parameter other than as the whole type (and a functional method's `self`, and varargs); an argument whose declared type mentions none is left to the binding, which converts it (rung C's `Coercions.coerce`); a type parameter that stands alone and that nothing else fixes takes the narrowest of its arguments' run-time types with their supertypes, the types a coercion takes them into (a reverse lookup of the lifted `coerce_` names at the top level of the library, of the function's component and of the value's type's component, `Coercions.coercionTargets`) and its bounds, that every one of its arguments is a subtype of or converts into; failing an instance that admits every argument, the answer is the old unification's, kept as `inferByUnification` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/EvaluatorBase.java:57-62`, `:75-304`). The reverse lookup's per-environment cache (`Coercions.coercionTypesByEnv`) is cleared per run by `Init.initializeEverything`, as the team's other static caches of interpreter objects are (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Init.java:44`). Arguments of one run-time type keep it (`T = Int` for two `ZZ32`s, row 364 unchanged); arguments of different types take the library's trait: `scale(b, z)` for `b: Box[\RR64\]` is `RR64` with `z` converted, `same(z, w)` and `lohi(z, w)` `ZZ64`, `pick(z, u)` with `u: NN32` `ZZ64`, `same(z, r)` `RR64`, `twice(l, z)` with `T extends Integral[\T\]` `ZZ64`, `pick(l, r)` `Number` with nothing converted (`ZZ64` into `RR64` stays explicit). The candidates are not only numbers': the rule reaches a user coercion into another argument's type, so `userS[\T\](a: T, b: T)` with `(AaaOf(1), CccOf(2))`, where `trait Aaa` declares `coerce(x: Ccc)`, runs at `T = Aaa` with the `CccOf` converted, where the stock compiled run converts nothing (`compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/probes/skeptic/walk-edit.txt:56-57`, `probes/skeptic/compiled.txt:117-119`; row 509). ℤ, ℤ64, ℤ32, ℕ64, ℕ32, ℚ and ℝ64 are siblings under `Number`, each a subtype of `Number` and none of another, with rung F's coercions: ℚ from the five integer types, ℝ64 from ℤ32 and integer numerals (answer 8's words), ℤ64 from ℤ32 and ℕ32, ℕ64 from ℕ32, ℤ from the four fixed widths, every other conversion explicit, the one into ℝ64 written `asFloat(x)` with the method the one library declares on `Number` (named at the gather, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:284`) (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-49`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:16-37`). The eighteen refined rational types and twelve refined integer types are gone: a subset is tested at run time, and the library's two checks are stated on ℝ64, `getter check(): Maybe[\RR64\]` and `getter check_star(): Maybe[\RR64\]` (`numbers.tex:51-65`). ℚ holds +∞, −∞ and 0/0, as the library's `Ratio` does (measured under walk, `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/examples/RatValues.walk.txt:3-10`) and as the operator chapter says of rational division by zero (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:166`), so its listing no longer claims a field or a total order; since climb batch 6.5 rung P (`581356f32`) it names the four algebraic traits the library declares on `QQ`, with the sentence that their laws hold for the finite rationals and need not hold where 0/0 or an infinity takes part (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:217-220`); the integer types hold no infinity. Answer 7's note is a callout at `Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`, scoped to the libraries the specification describes, with the compiled path's own smaller library, whose big operators take no static argument, named beside it; answer 8's rule, that a generic call over two integer types infers the narrowest type both coerce into, is a callout at `basic-integers.tex:80-94`, for a generic call only; until climb batch N it said such a call writes its static argument until the rule is written, and since batch N's rung T it points to the inference chapter, every range being over ℤ32 ("The specification's ranges are over ℤ32, and its own ranges over wider integer types are respelled" below); the automatic integer-to-float coercion is that of ℤ32 values and of integer numerals to ℝ64, and the coercion chapter's Example 1, a decimal integer literal for a floating-point parameter, stands (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:64-69`, `:158-159`). The integer `^` takes a ℤ exponent, and the chapter does not give the result of a negative power, which the Working Draft gave as a rational through ℚ (the callout at `basic-integers.tex:298-320`). Appendix I's entries I.1.10 to I.1.16 quote every original from the Working Draft of February 2011. - **The `XXX` expected-failure mechanism in `compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` can express a compile-stage failure only, and a run-time defect needs two `.test` files** (2026-09-20, rung B). `shouldFail` comes from the `.test` file name (`FileTests.java:932`) and the same flag reaches every stage the file drives (`:1052-1059`, `:1063-1069`), so an `XXX` file that carries `link` or `compile` demands that the compile fail (`:384-404`, message at `:402`); and a `TestTest` fails on an unsatisfied `run_out_*` verdict whatever `shouldFail` says (`:534-539`, `:583-585`), with `pass`/`PASS` demanded by default when no check is set (`:276-282`). Of the 224 `XXX*.test` files that were in `compiler_tests/` before this batch, 223 drive `compile`, one drives `link`, none drives `run`. A compiles-but-crashes defect is therefore gated as two `.test` files over one component — a plain-named one driving `link`, an `XXX`-named one driving `run` with a marker the failing run does print — which is what rung B did and showed going red on a deliberate fix (`compile-ladder/rung-tryatomic/raw/junit-xxx-expected.txt`, `raw/junit-xxx-goes-red.txt`), and what the gather reused for rung W's row 348.

### The specification and the repository's lineage

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § The specification and the repository's lineage: the POPL 2019 paper added as the type group's last published word on instantiation and dispatch, read from its full text (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, `reviews/decisions-review/popl-recheck.md`); the title, now false in part, kept, since entries are cited by it -->
- **The team's latest word on types and on the exclusion rule is the unfinished restart, not `Specification/`** (2026-09-26, `coordinator/spec-lineage.md` and its coordinator's check): `Documentation/Specification/` was begun 2012-02-20 (Luchangco, `166841592`) and abandoned 2012-05-31 with a 65-page build and mostly skeleton chapters; it was never adopted. Its Types chapter (`Prose/Language/types.tick`, Luchangco, 2012-05-31, `275b90773`) is from-scratch prose written a year and a half after `Specification/`'s last edit. It restates the rule as "instantiation exclusion" (:353-376), with a `\note` giving the stronger imposed form: a trait extending two instantiations must extend an expressible one below both. It adds a `covariant` modifier on trait static parameters (:320-339), where the older draft expresses covariance with a self-extending `where` clause (`trait-parameters.tex:339-352`). And it says `Bottom` is inexpressible (:173-195). On static parameters, traits, exceptions, components and the numeric library, `Specification/` is the only statement. "July 19, 2012" on our PDF is the date of the parentless import `5a68404fd`, chosen by the revival in `414b790e3`, not a date of any edit. `fortress.1.0.pdf` is the team's own 2008 artefact (`403afbe0b`), and the root `README.md:106-108` calls the directory beside it "the frozen Fortress 1.0 specification", which only the PDF is.

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § The specification and the repository's lineage: ℝ32 among the siblings stated as the present, and two narrations of change dropped -->
- **The specification's number chapters describe the flat library, and its advanced chapter on rational quantities is kept word for word as a superseded design** (climb batch 6 rung T, `d9c415395`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/decision-record.md`). ℤ, ℤ64, ℤ32, ℕ64, ℕ32, ℚ and ℝ64 are siblings under `Number` (ℝ32 beside them since climb batch 6.5b rung V, `e455ccd98`, with ℝ64's coercion from it, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:31`, `:43`, callout `:50-56`, Appendix I's "The single-precision floating-point type"), each a subtype of `Number` and none of another, with rung F's coercions: ℚ from the five integer types, ℝ64 from ℤ32 and integer numerals (answer 8's words), ℤ64 from ℤ32 and ℕ32, ℕ64 from ℕ32, ℤ from the four fixed widths, every other conversion explicit, the one into ℝ64 written `asFloat(x)` with the method the one library declares on `Number` (named at the gather, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:284`) (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-56`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:16-37`). The eighteen refined rational types and twelve refined integer types are gone: a subset is tested at run time, and the library's two checks are stated on ℝ64, `getter check(): Maybe[\RR64\]` and `getter check_star(): Maybe[\RR64\]` (`numbers.tex:58-72`). ℚ holds +∞, −∞ and 0/0, as the library's `Ratio` does (measured under walk, `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/examples/RatValues.walk.txt:3-10`) and as the operator chapter says of rational division by zero (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:166`), so its listing no longer claims a field or a total order; since climb batch 6.5 rung P (`581356f32`) it names the four algebraic traits the library declares on `QQ`, with the sentence that their laws hold for the finite rationals and need not hold where 0/0 or an infinity takes part (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:224-227`); the integer types hold no infinity. Answer 7's note is a callout at `Specification/basic/expressions/reductions.tex:27-44`, scoped to the libraries the specification describes, with the compiled path's own smaller library, whose big operators take no static argument, named beside it; answer 8's rule, that a generic call over two different integer types infers the narrowest type both coerce into, by the rule of the inference chapter, and need not write its static argument (`f(a, b)` for a ℤ32 `a` and a ℤ64 `b` infers ℤ64, as `f⟦ℤ64⟧(a, b)` writes it), is a callout at `basic-integers.tex:80-94`, for a generic call only, every range being over ℤ32 ("The specification's ranges are over ℤ32, and its own ranges over wider integer types are respelled" below); the automatic integer-to-float coercion is that of ℤ32 values and of integer numerals to ℝ64, and the coercion chapter's Example 1, a decimal integer literal for a floating-point parameter, stands (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:64-69`, `:158-159`). The integer `^` takes a ℤ exponent, and the chapter does not give the result of a negative power, which the Working Draft gave as a rational through ℚ (the callout at `basic-integers.tex:298-320`). Appendix I's entries I.1.10 to I.1.16 quote every original from the Working Draft of February 2011. The rung's own build has 620 pages; the gather checked the chapters against the landed library (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-6/RECORD.md`, rung T) and rebuilt the PDF on the merged tree, 621 pages (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/probes/build/gather-tex.txt`).

### Landed semantics

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § Landed semantics: the numeral switch's place brought to Pavol's decision of 2026-09-29, the split, in place of "rung Q's, in batch N's second run" -->
- **Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion, answer 8's promotion is walk's number case, and the declaration an overloaded call chooses is re-instantiated by it** (2026-09-29, climb batch N rung K, `041682188`; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md`). `EvaluatorBase.inferAndInstantiateGenericFunction` unifies, as before, only the arguments whose declared type mentions a static parameter other than as the whole type (and a functional method's `self`, and varargs); an argument whose declared type mentions none is left to the binding, which converts it (rung C's `Coercions.coerce`); a type parameter that stands alone and that nothing else fixes takes the narrowest of its arguments' run-time types with their supertypes, the types a coercion takes them into (a reverse lookup of the lifted `coerce_` names at the top level of the library, of the function's component and of the value's type's component, `Coercions.coercionTargets`) and its bounds, that every one of its arguments is a subtype of or converts into; failing an instance that admits every argument, the answer is the old unification's, kept as `inferByUnification` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/EvaluatorBase.java:57-62`, `:75-304`). The reverse lookup's per-environment cache (`Coercions.coercionTypesByEnv`) is cleared per run by `Init.initializeEverything`, as the team's other static caches of interpreter objects are (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Init.java:44`). Arguments of one run-time type keep it (`T = Int` for two `ZZ32`s, row 364 unchanged); arguments of different types take the library's trait: `scale(b, z)` for `b: Box[\RR64\]` is `RR64` with `z` converted, `same(z, w)` and `lohi(z, w)` `ZZ64`, `pick(z, u)` with `u: NN32` `ZZ64`, `same(z, r)` `RR64`, `twice(l, z)` with `T extends Integral[\T\]` `ZZ64`, `pick(l, r)` `Number` with nothing converted (`ZZ64` into `RR64` stays explicit). The candidates are not only numbers': the rule reaches a user coercion into another argument's type, so `userS[\T\](a: T, b: T)` with `(AaaOf(1), CccOf(2))`, where `trait Aaa` declares `coerce(x: Ccc)`, runs at `T = Aaa` with the `CccOf` converted, where the stock compiled run converts nothing (`compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/probes/skeptic/walk-edit.txt:56-57`, `probes/skeptic/compiled.txt:117-119`; row 509). A generic constructor takes the rule as a function does (`PairS(z, w)` builds `PairS[\ZZ64\]`). Row 388's flat-tower container shapes run at the nested tower's values, the container fixing `T` at `RR64` and the `ZZ32` scalar converted at binding: for an `RR64` array `a`, an `RR64` matrix `m` and `z: ZZ32 = 3`, `(a + z)[1]` and `(z + a)[1]` are `3.25`, `(a - z)[1]` `-2.75`, `(z - a)[1]` `2.75`, `(a MIN z)[0]` `1.5`, `(z MAX a)[0]` `3.0`, and `(m z)[0,0]`, `(z m)[0,0]` and `(m DOT z)[0,0]` `4.5`, all `RR64` (`ProjectFortress/tests/InferCoercionRungK.fss:59-67`). An overloaded call chooses as before, on the join instantiation (`bestMatchInternal`, `values/OverloadedFunction.java:879-929`), and the chosen generic declaration is instantiated again by the rule before it is applied, so `op(z, w)` for `op[\T extends Number\](a: T, b: T)` beside `op(a: Any, b: Any)` runs the generic at `ZZ64` (the conversion rule, POSITIONS 2026-09-28); the coercion pass keeps generic declarations (`og(b, z)` beside `og(b: String, x: String)` is the generic at `RR64`), and a generic trait's coercion is instantiated with the target's own static arguments (`Coercions.coercionFor`, row 389), except a coercion that declares its own static parameter, which walk still refuses (`coerce[\S\](x: TagR[\S\])` in `trait WideR[\T\]`; row 513, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionOwnStaticRungK.fss`). Where a static type is wider than its value, walk now runs the generic at the narrower instance the compiled run does not (`O2Wide`'s `op(n, w)`: compiled `T = Number`, walk `ZZ64`; row 509). Not reached: a type fixed through a structure (`SUM <|1, 2, 3|>`, row 432), a `nat` parameter at an `NN32` binding (row 486), the expected type at a generic result (`a: BoxK[\ZZ64\] = wrapK(3)`, row 510), a varargs parameter `T...` and a tuple parameter `(T, T)` over mixed widths, which stay at the join unconverted (row 511), a numeral alone at a bound it does not meet (walk's numeral is a `ZZ32`; the numeral switch is rung Q's, in batch N's second run). ### The container

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § The container: the incidents of 2026-09-27, 09-28 (twice) and 09-29 (twice), appended one after another, restated as what a restart stops and keeps, how a run is resumed, what the cache needs and what a stage stopped mid-work leaves, each rule with the incident that shows it; "the cause is not visible from inside", which the cap's entry answers, dropped -->
- **A restart of the session's own process kills its background runs, and `resumeFromRunId` then recovers every agent that had finished** (2026-09-27, session `fe616d40`). At 12:09:17 UTC the environment manager restarted the session's Claude Code process (`environment-manager task-run … --session-mode resume`; the VM itself was not restarted, `uptime -s` still 2026-09-26 23:11:31, kernel fc-v37); the cause is not visible from inside. Batch 6b's run `wf_08949b8a-a21` and an `Agent`-tool worker died with it: the run's repair agent's transcript ends 12:09, four minutes into its stage. The conversation, worktrees, untracked files and transcripts survived. A relaunch from the base (12:12, `wf_2da3e152-2d5`) restarted at the first stage; the same script and arguments with `resumeFromRunId: wf_08949b8a-a21` (12:20) took rung O's worker, skeptic and judge from the old run's `journal.jsonl` without running them and started the repair stage anew. The resume reuses the longest unchanged prefix of the run's `agent()` calls in call order, so it needs the launch's arguments byte for byte and the same order of calls (the stop of 2026-09-28 at 20:34 below). So after a death that leaves the session, its ID and the run's journal in place, the run is resumed with the script text and arguments of its launch, not relaunched; a finished agent's result is kept, an unfinished one runs from its start, and its worktree's leftovers are its starting point. A run whose script has changed since launch is resumed from a copy of the script as launched (`git show <base>:<path>`); where cached stages resolve at once and a pipeline would call its next stage in another order than the live run did, from a copy that forces the live run's order, prompts unchanged. What does not carry over is a new session: `remote-container.md` § The 2026-09-18 restart and step 5 of the recovery list. The same restart undid a compaction: the resumed process rebuilt the conversation from the transcript as if the manual compaction of 08:40 had not happened, from the one of 03:28 on, so the context the model saw went from 421K on the last call before the restart to 802K on the first after it with nothing new in the chat, and the automatic compaction fired at 12:11 at 805K. Measured: the 12:11 boundary's `cumulativeDroppedTokens`, 8,783,976, is the 03:28 boundary's 7,994,881 plus its own 789,095, leaving out the 08:40 compaction's 741,537, and the 03:28 boundary record appears a second time in the transcript at the reload (lines 25826 and 32220); what the reload sent beyond that is inferred, not shown (`explorations/reviews/coordinator-context-2026-09-27.md`, `e15e1a01a`). After a restart of the session's process, `/context` shows whether it happened again. It happened again on 2026-09-28: the session's process started anew at 07:36:42 UTC, the VM not restarted (`uptime -s` still 2026-09-27 18:39:21). Batch 7R's run, three `Agent`-tool workers and the push loop stopped, while shell scripts the workers had started in the background kept running (probe K's `run-all.sh`, started 05:51, and a comparison pass of rung J's). The run was resumed at 07:38 with the same script and arguments and `resumeFromRunId`: rung U's worker and skeptic came from the journal, and rung J's worker started anew under the same key. The `Agent`-tool workers continued from their transcripts on a `SendMessage`. It happened a third time the same day: the signal came at 20:34:04 UTC and the process started anew at 20:34:07 (`/tmp/env-manager.log`), stopping batch 6.5's first run, `wf_fa14416d-889`, in its judge stage, whose agent's transcript ends at 20:33:18. Two resumes missed. The base given as the short hash where the launch had given the full hash missed the cache from the first call: rungs G and P started anew at 20:34:46 (the run's `journal.jsonl`, lines 17-18, against 2-3). With the base as launched, the rungs' cached results resolved at once and the pipeline called skeptic G before skeptic P, where the live run had called P, then G, and both started anew at 20:35:35 (lines 19-20, against 5 and 7). A copy of the script as launched that forces the original order, prompts unchanged (`scratchpad/wf-6.5-run1-resume.js` in the session's scratchpad), recovered every finished agent, the two rungs, the two skeptics, the gather, the gate and the review, and started the judge anew under its old key at 20:37:53 (line 21, against 15; `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/subagents/workflows/wf_fa14416d-889/`). Climb batch N's first run, `wf_4ba3c084-2b3`, ended unlanded and was resumed three times on 2026-09-29 with copies of its script (`scratchpad/wf-N-run1-resume.js`, `wf-N-run1-land-first-gate.js` in the session's scratchpad), each wrapping `agent()` so that the 23 finished calls are issued in the journal's order of their `started` lines (`RESUME_ORDER` and `orderedAgent`); every one came from the journal. A copy that changes only what follows the cached prefix (there the gate skipped and the commit's prompt extended) runs the changed call live and nothing before it. The stop of 09:31:56 killed that commit stage before it had committed: its edits were in the main tree, uncommitted, and a resume whose commit prompt named them (a changed prompt, so a new key) checked and kept them and landed the batch (`3fb0cd8c1`, the run's journal, lines 49-51). The run's journal is `journal.jsonl` in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/`: one `launched` line, then a `started` line per agent call (`key`, `agentId`, `label`, `phase`) and a `result` line with the same key and the agent's structured result, none for an agent that returned nothing; a resumed run appends to the same journal, and an agent run live again under a key the journal holds gets a second `started` line (`coordinator/tools/journal-text.py`, which reads it). Climb batch 6.5b's run, `wf_07b95462-a7d`, was killed in its gather by the VM restart of 2026-09-29 at 14:35 UTC (the VM entry above). The gather's partial staged state was stashed (`stash@{0}`) and its untracked rung directory moved aside, and the run was resumed at 14:40 with the script as launched and `resumeFromRunId`: the finished agents came from the journal and the gather ran again live from its start under its key, the journal's two `gather` lines under one `launched` line; the landing needed nothing from the stash, which was dropped after it (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-6.5b/RECORD.md`, "A relaunched gather").

<!-- moved 2026-09-29 from FACTS.md § The container: the stops restated as the cap's evidence and the present: the last start and the next stop -->
- **The platform stops the session's process after about 12 hours 58 minutes of continuous running, and restarts it in resume mode within seconds** (2026-09-28, the environment manager's log `/tmp/env-manager.log`, read by the coordinator). Every stop in the log is a `SIGTERM` from outside ("Received signal, shutting down gracefully", signal `terminated`, 138 since 2026-09-08), followed by "Claude Code stopped due to context cancellation" with the run's length, then "Set session mode for environment" `resume`. Five runs ended at nearly the same length, 46,636 to 46,660 s (12 h 57 min 16 s to 12 h 57 min 40 s): 2026-09-20 03:45:13, 09-26 22:02:00, 09-27 12:09:17, 09-28 07:36:42 and 09-28 20:34:06 UTC; the rest are short runs of a few minutes to a few hours that end when the session goes idle. So the restarts of 09-27 12:09, 09-28 07:36 and 09-28 20:34 ("A restart of the session's own process ..." above) were this cap, not a crash, not memory and not a message; they fall while Pavol is talking because the process runs continuously only while he or a check-in keeps it busy. Any restart, a VM start included, resets the clock, so the next stop is predictable: the last start plus 12 h 58 min. The second stop of 09-28 confirmed it: its signal came at 20:34:04, 12 h 57 min after the start of 07:36:43, and the process started again at 20:34:07. A check-in armed a few minutes after that time resumes what the stop killed. The first stop of 2026-09-29 came at 09:31:56 UTC, 12 h 57 min 49 s after the start of 20:34:07. The day's second stop, at 14:35:43 UTC, was a VM restart after a run of 18,226 s, not this cap (the last start was 09:31:58; `uptime -s` 14:36:58); the process started again at 14:37:16, so the next stop falls near 03:35 UTC on 2026-09-30.

- **The hidden layer, classified: 203 errors once the early ones clear, and batch 3 lands at 23** (2026-09-22, `perf-probes/nat/triage.md`, captures and `make-fixes.py` under `triage/`). The zero worker's 173 was unstable because a memo in the overloading checker keyed on declaration pairs (`OverloadingChecker.scala:441-462`) hides 27-35 errors depending on build order; with the tree's own switch `fortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false` every build gives 203. None of the 203 is the exclusion relation (relaxing exclusion clears nothing; the strong `checkP` adds 284). ### Landed semantics

## Replaced 2026-09-30, at climb batch 7b's gather (rung W's record)

<!-- replaced in FACTS.md § Execution model by rung W's three entries, "Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains ..." among them, as its record asks: the cache key now holds each static parameter's kind and bounds, row 478 fixed -->
- **Walk's overload check reads one bound for two generic overloads whose static parameters share a name** (2026-09-28, climb batch 7R rung J; `compile-ladder/rung-ranges-zz32/probes/rangeoperators/`; row 478). Walk caches one symbolic instantiation per generic function in `symbolicStaticsByPartition` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FGenericFunction.java:43-62`, under the team's "TODO This is not quite right"). The key is the function's name and its static parameters, compared by name alone (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:44-58`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java:402-404`). Generic constructors share the cache (`GenericConstructor.java:170-178`). So of two overloads `f[\I extends AnyIntegral\](x:I, y:I)` and `f[\I\](x:I, y:I, z:I)` beside `f(x:String, y:String)`, one takes the other's bound. Walk refuses the set with the bounded one declared first and accepts it in the other order; it accepts both orders once the unbounded one's parameter is named `J` (`BoundBoundedFirstSameName.txt` against the other three captures). On the base, `rangeOperators.fss` passed only because the kept `opr #[\I\](r: PartialRange[\I\], size:I)` borrowed `AnyIntegral`, which excludes `String`, from `opr #[\I extends AnyIntegral\](lo:I, ex:I)` (`ro-trace.txt`). After rung J it passes because `Range` excludes `String`. The check between a program's declaration and the library's runs only for a name the program declares at least twice (FACTS, "The library's scalar extension is eight generic declarations"), and only on a run that analyses `FortressLibrary` afresh (rows 98, 342).

### Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- Two execution paths share parser and phases and differ at the end: the walk interpreter (`fortress file.fss`) and the bytecode compiler (`fortress compile` + `run`) (`repo-internals.md:95-129`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- The static type checker (Scala, `scala_src/typechecker/`) runs only on the compile path; `walk` turns it off and there is no switch to make it run in the interpreter (`repo-internals.md:127`); every "type error" seen from the interpreter is a run-time dispatch failure.

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- `fortress typecheck` checks against `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, not the interpreter's prelude, so it is not an oracle for interpreter programs (ledger row 69); making the checker usable on interpreter programs means giving it the interpreter's prelude, which is not a ledger row and not on the worklist as a separate item (it falls under worklist item 2, compiler-path library parity).

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- On microGPT-shaped array code boxing is the dominant representational cost, 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]` in Java models of the program's three kernels, and nothing microGPT-shaped compiles: the compiler prelude lacks the array types, with `Array`, `Vector` and `Array3` undefined in `FlatArrays.fsi` (row 305, wider than row 72). On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The two one-line runtime defects it found are fixed (rows 302, 303; rung 0, `53362cb88`), and no array type goes into the compiler prelude: the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (POSITIONS 2026-09-21, the library route). A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`258105b3e`; `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`).

- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`), and its descriptor in a stamped class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` since climb batch 5 rung Z (`e893a3e00`).

- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below): so it stood until climb batch 4 rung N (`3f297441c`), since which it checks `nat` and `int` static parameters ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below), and since climb batch 5 rung Z (`e893a3e00`) a sized program loads and runs compiled ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** The Working Draft's `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`, kept since climb batch 5 rung S in `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:61-65` marked "Not allowed") stops on both paths with a syntax error at `excludes`, because the grammar gives an object no `excludes` clause (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:84-86`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothing.fss` and its captures). Without that clause, `fortress compile` and `fortress walk` give the identical single error, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothingNoExcludes.fss`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4093`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind the library's comment on its parametric `Nothing[\T\]`, "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working" (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1449-1450`), and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (2026-09-20, rung X). `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it — a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" — and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (2026-09-22, rung C, `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only. A declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. So a comment-only edit to the library is not neutral at the syntax-tree level: rung C's widened three spans (the scalar block's first `-` in both files, `SUFFIX_SUM` in the `.fsi`), besides shifting every position below each insertion, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics must map positions back first (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py`, `remap-lines.py`). No answer changed.

- **Walk's overload check reads one bound for two generic overloads whose static parameters share a name** (2026-09-28, climb batch 7R rung J; `compile-ladder/rung-ranges-zz32/probes/rangeoperators/`; row 478). Walk caches one symbolic instantiation per generic function in `symbolicStaticsByPartition` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/FGenericFunction.java:43-62`, under the team's "TODO This is not quite right"). The key is the function's name and its static parameters, compared by name alone (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:44-58`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java:402-404`). Generic constructors share the cache (`GenericConstructor.java:170-178`). So of two overloads `f[\I extends AnyIntegral\](x:I, y:I)` and `f[\I\](x:I, y:I, z:I)` beside `f(x:String, y:String)`, one takes the other's bound. Walk refuses the set with the bounded one declared first and accepts it in the other order; it accepts both orders once the unbounded one's parameter is named `J` (`BoundBoundedFirstSameName.txt` against the other three captures). On the base, `rangeOperators.fss` passed only because the kept `opr #[\I\](r: PartialRange[\I\], size:I)` borrowed `AnyIntegral`, which excludes `String`, from `opr #[\I extends AnyIntegral\](lo:I, ex:I)` (`ro-trace.txt`). After rung J it passes because `Range` excludes `String`. The check between a program's declaration and the library's runs only for a name the program declares at least twice (FACTS, "The library's scalar extension is eight generic declarations"), and only on a run that analyses `FortressLibrary` afresh (rows 98, 342).

- **The compiled run's class loader takes its first load of a name under the JDK's class-loading lock, and a generic arm's first load is safe on four threads** (2026-09-28, climb batch 6.5 rung G, `fd5cb4864`; `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1, 11, 12; row 417). `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` runs under `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, as the JDK's own `ClassLoader.loadClass` does (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/jdk-loadclass-javap.txt:2-9`). No loader in the tree registers as parallel-capable, so that lock is the loader's own monitor, the one the JVM already holds when it resolves a class through the loader. The explicit loads, `RTHelpers.loadClosureClass`, `RTHelpers.getRTTIclass` and the union instantiation, had been the only ones without it. `history` is still written before `defineClass`, safe under the lock. Measured: `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG` fails 5 of 5 compiled runs at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` on the base and passes 5 of 5 after (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/threads-before.txt:10-14`, `threads-after.txt:10-14`). The compiled path's channel is Chase's run of 2011-12-08 to 2012-01-30: `a5a06c65c` the heavy-angle name channel and `oprArgAnnotatedRTTI`; `3b7bda65e` the six kind tags `XL_BOOL`/`XL_INTNAT`/`XL_OPR`/`XL_TYPE`/`XL_UNIT`/`XL_DIM` born together (`runtimeSystem/Naming.java:212-217`); `bcf08dae8` `isOprKind`, the run time's only kind predicate, under the message "still busted"; `49e0373b8` `RTTI.java` itself, the descriptor base class, built to make the opr case work. An operator's slot in a descriptor factory is filled with null ("Push nulls for opr parameters in the factory call", `InstantiatingClassloader.java:2683`) and nothing reads it; no site on either path dispatches on, compares or type-tests an operator argument; nothing in `Papers/` or the run time's comments discusses unifying the kinds. Neither library declares an `opr` static parameter; `ProjectFortress/tests/conditionalExtension.fss` and `compiler_tests/XXXOprParamRungS.fss` are its only uses. - **The compiled checker does not enforce the specification's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters; forced past the api's early return, its overloading check reports 482 errors on the one library, and four defects sit on the way** (2026-09-26, `reviews/overload-static-params-ways.md` §§ 2-3, a clean worker; 25 two-path probes and captures under `reviews/overload-static-params-ways/`). The title's 482 is the nested tower's, measured by forcing; since climb batch 7C's rung Y the api's overloading and return-type checks run on the count stage, where the flat library's `FortressLibrary` api adds 66 (61 overloading, 5 return type; "The true distance to the switch-over" below). The checker applies the Types paper's rules and refuses only pairs it cannot prove: open traits, and `CAP`, whose domains exclude only through the exclusion rule plus a bound, a step it lacks. Forced past the `FortressLibrary` api's early return (a guarded copy of `StaticChecker.java`), the overloading check reports 482 errors: 421 in `FortressLibrary`, 39 in `RangeInternals`, 22 in `NativeArray`. By the two arms' static parameters: different lists 29; one generic and one plain 137; same list 58; both plain 215; duplicates 43. All 132 generic-plus-plain return-type errors and the 43 duplicates have a plain arm on a tower or `Comparison` type that the checker reports as excluding its own supertypes (`FortressLibrary.fsi:121`, `:373`, `:438`, `:465`); the worker reads these as artefacts the flattening removes, not re-run on a flat library. The four defects: walk's choice between a generic and a plain arm depends on declaration order (`OverloadedFunction.java:871-892`); the return-type rule checks one solved instance where the paper asks for all (`OverloadingOracle.scala:81-117`), so the paper's own counterexample passes and fails the JVM verifier and a permuted override throws `ClassCastException` (row 398); code generation fails for two generic arms on a bare type variable; walk runs an arm whose static parameter is in no parameter type with that parameter unbound, while the compiled path never chooses it (row 400). The sentence dates from 2009-10; the 1.0 release of 2008 compared generic arms by their bounds; the later restart's overloading chapter omits the sentence. - **The flattening's three questions, measured by a clean worker** (2026-09-26, `reviews/flattening-questions-ways.md`, about 30 probes and captures under `reviews/flattening-questions-ways/`). *The empty sum.* The interpreter's empty sum is `0 : Int` for every element type. A one-reduction-per-element-type design reached from one generic declaration is the library's own pattern (`BitXor`, `MINNUM`, `CompilerLibrary`'s `ZZ32Addition`, the specification's `SumZZ32`). But a no-argument form cannot be overloaded by result type alone (measured), and the library's way around it, a static parameter plus a `typecase` over a `() -> T` witness, works under walk and is rejected by the compiled checker as written. C4 needs a `ZZ32` zero for `matOffset(0)` (`run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fss:43`), `RR64` results for `SUM e`, `SUM vm` and `DOT`, and `RR64`'s own `MAX`. *Mixed widths.* On the nested tower, under walk a variable declared `ZZ64` that held a literal did 32-bit arithmetic (`a + b = -2147483648`, the defect in the exclusion fork's entry above, row 146, closed by climb batch 6 rung F), and a range from 2^31-1 to a `ZZ64` enumerated wrapped `Int`s. The compiled checker with its own prelude infers a union for a generic call over mixed widths, which crashed code generation. The note did not reach the checker over the one library; on the flat library both paths take for such a call the narrowest type its arguments convert into and convert them, answer 8's promotion ("Static arguments are inferred from the arguments alone, on both paths, and never through a coercion" below). The two programs have no `ZZ64` variables, but they need `ZZ32`-to-`RR64` and literal-to-`RR64` coercions, which the compiled prelude lacks and the one library has: the programs' `1.0 s` and `1 - beta1` shapes are `RR64` on both paths against it (`reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` § 7.1). *`RationalQuantity`.* The compiled checker rejects it ("Cyclic type hierarchy") and walk cannot instantiate it. The library never had it or any sign-refined type. *History, correcting the record's attribution:* the compiler prelude's tower was not flattened by Steele in 2011. David Chase cut the subtyping on 2009-08-31 (`6896886fb`), Sukyoung Ryu added the exclusions (`3e0306166`, 2009-10-16), the coercions came in 2009-2010, and Steele built the operators on the flat prelude later (the note's Question 1 § 7). POSITIONS 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 carry the earlier attribution in the record's words at the time.

- **The coercions between number types carry a sum's zero and a product's one into every wider type by themselves, and not a maximum's identity** (2026-09-26, `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement.md` §§ 1-2, probes and captures under `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement/`). A coercion keeps the arithmetic, so the converted zero and one are the wider type's own, measured on both paths: on walk with `widen`, for a `ZZ64` `y` below `ZZ32`'s range, `widen(0) + y` and `widen(1) y` give `y`, and into `RR64` `0 + (-1.0e300)` gives `-1.0e300` (`MaxMinWalk.walk.txt` § 5); compiled, where the coercion is real, `s: ZZ64 = SUM[j <- 0#0] j` holds `ZZ32`'s zero converted and `s + y` gives `y` (`MaxComp.comp.txt`). A maximum's identity is the type's least element (a minimum's its greatest), which a coercion does not carry: the smallest `ZZ32` widened, `MAX` `y`, gives -2147483648, not `y` (walk), and compiled `m: ZZ64 = BIG MAX[j <- 0#0] j` holds -2147483648 with `m MAX y = m`; `ZZ` and `QQ` have no least element. The library's generic `BIG MAX` has no identity, and an empty one raises `EmptyReduction`, which the team's test asserts (`ProjectFortress/tests/simpleSum.fss:56-60`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2907-2927`, `:3117-3147`); its one extremum with an identity is `BIG MAXNUM`/`BIG MINNUM`, `RR64` only, NaN. Under answer 7 the identity is made at the fold's own type, so no identity is coerced inside a reduction. The three `Number`-typed `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `BIG MINMAXN` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3076-3114` at the judgement's base), whose identity was the rational `-1/0` for every element type and which had no caller, were dropped by climb batch 6 rung F (`d846e3644`; POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the three `Number`-typed big operators). The judgement's library slips are ledger rows 421-423, row 423 closed by the drop.

The first attempt is by subtyping under the expected type and counts only candidates without a coercion the call needs; a declaration that fits the call's arguments but whose result the expected type refuses is not among its candidates. A call no attempt keeps takes the first attempt holding a candidate: for a call written `f(x)`, among the attempts without the context, so that the binding reports a call the rule accepts; for any other call, among those with it, which keeps today's message (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:604-752`; `Operators.scala:85`, `:90`, `:197`, `:345`). **The coercion attempt** (`checkApplicableWithCoercion`, `Functionals.scala:280-400`). An `RR32` with an `RR64`, a float numeral or a `ZZ32` converts to `RR64` and answers an `RR64`, as the specification's example computes (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:904-912`). An `RR32` bound to an `RR64` variable or parameter converts, and so does one stored in an `RR64` field or array element or assigned to an `RR64` variable, but not one returned from a body declared `RR64`, since walk checks no declared return (row 387; its skeptic's `compile-ladder/rung-rr32-sibling/probes/skeptic/SkCtx.edit.txt`). A generic `T` over an `RR32` and an `RR64` is `RR64` by answer 8's promotion. `=`, `<` and `CMP` with an `RR64` answer. Nothing coerces into `RR32`, and `narrow` stays explicit. *The specification.* `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:27-56` names `ℝ32` among the number types and `ℝ64`'s coercion from it, with a callout. Appendix I's entry "The single-precision floating-point type" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1714-1790`) revises batch 6's sentence that `ℝ32` stays below `ℝ64` (`:485-487`); the reasoning is in `compile-ladder/rung-rr32-sibling/decision-record.md`. *The gates and measurements.* Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/RR32SiblingRungV.fss` (37 assertions) and by row 435's promoted `ProjectFortress/tests/RR32MixedRungF.fss`. <!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § The specification and the repository's lineage: rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **The team's latest word on types and on the exclusion rule is the unfinished restart, not `Specification/`** (2026-09-26, `coordinator/spec-lineage.md` and its coordinator's check): `Documentation/Specification/` was begun 2012-02-20 (Luchangco, `166841592`) and abandoned 2012-05-31 with a 65-page build and mostly skeleton chapters; it was never adopted. Its Types chapter (`Prose/Language/types.tick`, Luchangco, 2012-05-31, `275b90773`) is from-scratch prose written a year and a half after `Specification/`'s last edit. It restates the rule as "instantiation exclusion" (:353-376), with a `\note` giving the stronger imposed form: a trait extending two instantiations must extend an expressible one below both. It adds a `covariant` modifier on trait static parameters (:320-339), where the older draft expresses covariance with a self-extending `where` clause (`trait-parameters.tex:339-352`). And it says `Bottom` is inexpressible (:173-195). On static parameters, traits, exceptions, components and the numeric library, `Specification/` is the only statement. "July 19, 2012" on our PDF is the date of the parentless import `5a68404fd`, chosen by the revival in `414b790e3`, not a date of any edit. `fortress.1.0.pdf` is the team's own 2008 artefact (`403afbe0b`), and the root `README.md:106-108` calls the directory beside it "the frozen Fortress 1.0 specification", which only the PDF is. Later than both is the type group's last published word on instantiation and dispatch: Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, "Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance", PACMPL 3, POPL 2019, Article 11 (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, read from the full text; the review of Pavol's decisions rechecked against it, `reviews/decisions-review/popl-recheck.md`). At run-time dispatch a type parameter that nothing fixes takes the intersection of its upper bounds, its declared bound and the constraint of the call's static return type, and the solver never instantiates it at `Bottom` (p. 11:19); the team's earlier assumption, the union of the lower bounds, the authors could not prove (p. 11:25). Of static inference the paper asks only that it instantiate at non-`Bottom` types (pp. 11:16-17), gives no algorithm (p. 11:25), and annotates its one static example, `O.m(3, true)`, at the union `Int ⊔ Boolean` (p. 11:21). The run-time check of the return type chooses the instance, never the declaration (Lemmas 5.8 and 5.9, pp. 11:22-23): Naden's second write-up's proposal (`Papers/RuntimeInstantiation/RTRinstantionTheory.tex:73-80`), not the static context limiting which declarations apply, which his first rejected (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:241-305`). A type parameter's default bounds are `Any` and `Bottom` (p. 11:9). No method type parameter may appear in an upper bound (p. 11:11), so the paper's soundness theorem does not cover the library's F-bounded functions, `SUM`, `BIG MAX` and those over `Integral[\I\]`. Theorem 4.1 keeps static uniqueness, a unique most specific declaration for every call (p. 11:15); the exclusion rule is [Anc-Same-Trait], a class that extends two instances of a trait extends an instance below both (p. 11:11), blanket for an invariant parameter; and [D-Method] keeps a covariant parameter out of parameter positions, so no self-typed algebra trait can be covariant (`Equality[\+T\]`; the recheck's § 1.1). It has no closed types, nominal exclusion, modules or top-level functions (pp. 11:3, 11:25), and no coercion or numbers. The paper is CC BY-NC 4.0; its PDF and its text stay in the gitignored `research/decks/`. Its instance rule is Pavol's decision (POSITIONS 2026-09-29, a type parameter that a call's arguments do not fix), and the checker's `Bottom` binding it replaces is "Keeping the expected type at a call written `f(x)` ..." under The checker and the one library.

- **The specification states the integer rules of 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-24, the coercion example with the exclusions its definition needs, and the rational type's library algebra** (2026-09-28, climb batch 6.5 rung P, `581356f32`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md`). The integer chapter's opening states `narrow` (the low 32 bits of a `ZZ64`, `ZZ` or `NN64`) and `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on the five integer types: on a fixed width `n` and a count `k >= 0`, `x RSHIFT k` is `floor(x/2^k)` and `x LSHIFT k` is `x 2^k` reduced into the type modulo `2^n`, a negative count shifting the other way, the count of any integer type read by its value, and on `ZZ` the two are `shift(x,k)` and `shift(x,-k)` (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-66`). The entry of `shift` adds that it is exact at any count and that a result too large for the implementation throws `IntegerOverflow` (`:725-730`). `GCD` and `LCM` give the absolute value of the other argument where the Working Draft said the other argument, with the property `(m GCD n)(m LCM n) = abs(m n)` (`:541-568`). The operator overview adds that both results are nonnegative and that a result a fixed-size type cannot hold throws `IntegerOverflow`, and it names the shifts among the bitwise operators (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:262-270`, `:341-344`). The coercion chapter's example declares `ZZ32 excludes { ZZ64, ZZ128 }` and `ZZ64 excludes { ZZ128 }`, as the library spells its integer exclusions, and both paths run it as printed (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:556-597`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/probes/examples/SpecZZExcl.walk.txt`, `SpecZZExcl.compiled.txt`; row 394). `QQ`'s listing extends the library's `StandardPartialOrder`, `StandardMinMax`, `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing` at `QQ`, with one sentence that their laws hold for the finite rationals and need not hold where 0/0 or an infinity takes part, as those of the same traits on `RR64` need not hold where a NaN takes part (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:99-101`, `:152-154`, `:224-231`). - **The specification's type-inference chapter states the rule of climb batch N** (climb batch N rung T; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/decision-record.md`). `Specification/basic/inference.tex:15-236` describes the inference of a call's static arguments for type parameters and for `nat` and `int` parameters only (`:19-25`). For a call of a function, a method, an operator or a generic constructor that does not write its static arguments, the declaration is chosen first, as the coercion chapter's resolution chooses it, a declaration with static parameters applicable when some instance within its bounds is and compared on its declared parameter types, so a coercion never changes which declaration is chosen when one applies without it (`:60-69`); its static arguments are then inferred: a type, `nat` or `int` parameter inside a parameter type fixed by that argument by subtyping, a type parameter inside the declared return type by the expected type, a type parameter that is the whole type of parameters taking among its arguments' types and the types they coerce to the narrowest under ⪯ that all are substitutable for and its bounds permit (for numbers the narrowest type all convert into, ℤ64 for ℤ32 with ℕ32), otherwise the union of their types with nothing converted; every argument admitted by substitutability, the coercions inserted statically (`:71-106`); the expected type from a variable or field declaration that declares its type, an assignment to a variable whose type is declared, a declared return type, a block's last expression where no local declaration precedes it and both branches of an `if … else`, used at `f(x)`, a method invocation or an operator, with a retry without it when the result converts (`:108-134`); the converted call dispatching by subtyping to the most specific declaration applicable to the converted values (`:136-139`). A numeral whose conversions tie is read as ℤ32, or ℤ64 or ℤ by its value, in either step; a tie a non-numeral argument makes among declarations applicable only with coercion is a static error (`:162-185`, `\seclabel{numeral-default}`). Not described (`:187-210`): the static arguments of a `bool`, `dim`, `unit` or operator parameter, a static parameter nothing fixes (the BottomType question left open), a conversion inside a structured argument, the expected type in other contexts, a generic object named without a call, whole-program inference. Three callouts: the bound `Any` assumed where `trait-parameters.tex:49-50` says `Object` (and the compiled path takes `Object`, row 412), the overloading chapter's three sentences and the naked-Any rule left to batch 7b's rung S (`:26-51`); the interpreter's run-time rule (`:149-160`); and (`:211-224`) for a type parameter only the return type mentions and that the expected type does not fix, the compiled checker binds it to `BottomType` except that it refuses a call with no expected type when the parameter is declared `extends Any`, and the interpreter erases such a parameter of a function to `BottomType` and leaves a generic method's uninstantiated; neither implementation infers a `bool` parameter (the checker refuses a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` one by name, walk does not unify a `bool` one), though the Working Draft's `bool` example (`trait-parameters.tex:117-119`) can be applied only if its argument fixes the parameter. The ranges section says a `nat` or `int` parameter used as a component converts to ℤ32 as an integer numeral does (`Specification/basic/expressions/ranges.tex:46-58`), which both paths ran on the base (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/probes/examples/SizeAsComponent-base.txt`). Appendix I's I.1.25 quotes every original (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1550-1712`). Built at 635 pages on the rung's tree, 631 before, with the base's warnings (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-inference/probes/build/`); 637 on the merged tree, whose Part IV also carries rung M's fifteen api declarations (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/build/`). Checked at the gather against rung I's landed checker, statement by statement (the decision record, section 6; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/RECORD.md`, rung T): statements 1 to 3, 6 to 11 and 13 hold, and 4 except `ZZ32` with `NN32`, which is `ZZ` on the compiler prelude (row 442); statement 12 does not hold at `f(x)` or at an operator (row 508); statement 5 does not hold for a coerced argument beside a lone type parameter with no narrowest type, which the checker refuses (row 515), nor under a written trait bound, which both implementations take where the chapter gives the union (row 516; the judge ruled that decision 1 settles it for the union, and each implementation carries its expected failure, `XXXInferLoneBoundUnion` and `XXXInferLoneUnionWalk`, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/JUDGE-review.md` section 1); the interpreter's callout stands, rung K having landed, except that it does not yet say walk binds a named common supertype where the rule gives a union.
