- The transcript backup fires on the main session's Stop, not on any agent's completion, so a session inside one long turn is not being backed up. Its Stop hook returns at once (0.01 s in the change's own test, where every turn had waited 24-27 s plus the push) and leaves the work to a detached runner, which copies, commits, pushes whenever the branch is ahead of its upstream and packs (`gc --auto` at `gc.auto=1000`), one line per pass in `/home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/.backup.log`, the last 200 kept; a pass takes about 10 s, the copier about 1 s of it. The copier is incremental on size and modification time (`.backup.state`), and its output is byte for byte the old copier's (1,012 files, 958 MB, `diff -r`). Workflow agents' transcripts are among its sources, and a transcript over 64 MiB is split. It swallows every error and never holds up the session, so a failed push shows only in the log's `push=` field. A container that dies within about 10 s of a turn's end loses that turn's snapshot; only an `index.lock` at least 10 s old that no process has open is cleaned, and a stale `/home/user/fortress/.git/refs/heads/transcripts-blinded.lock` fails every later commit (`commit=failed`) until it is removed by hand. Snapshots before the change can be missing: a detached gc inherited the runner's lock and held it while it ran, and every snapshot requested meanwhile was skipped. (`transcripts-blinded@974d9be7`, its message; `coordinator/remote-container.md` § How the snapshot works; the reference copies in `coordinator/transcript-backup/`.) The platform's own Stop hook, `~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh`, comes from the launcher's `--settings /root/.claude/launcher-settings.json` and is rewritten at every process start; it exits 2, which makes the session take another turn, whenever the tree has uncommitted changes, untracked files, or unpushed or unverifiable commits. At Pavol's request of 2026-09-29 it is a no-op, the original kept in the session scratchpad (`stop-hook-git-check.sh.orig`); it returns at each restart of the process, and turning it off again is Pavol's to do in manual mode, since the auto-mode check refused to schedule it ("The session's automatic permission check refuses a step ..." below). The push loop covers what it protected ("The push loop pushes `main` every 4 minutes ..." below).

### Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: added at climb batch 7b's gather (rung W); rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains, so the order they are written in no longer decides** (2026-09-29, climb batch 7b rung W, `8f7e183d4`; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 5.1; answer 9, POSITIONS 2026-09-26). `OverloadedFunction.bestMatchInternal` keeps a candidate by `moreSpecificDeclaration` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:1335-1342`). When one of two applicable declarations is a generic function or constructor with static parameters of its own, their declared domains are compared: the symbolic instantiation, each type parameter standing for itself with its bounds as supertypes, and a domain lies inside a generic one when walk's inference finds an instance holding it from values that carry only its types (`instanceHolding`, `:1291-1306`). Otherwise, as for two plain declarations, their instances' domains are compared. A functional method of a generic trait and a generic dotted method keep the instance comparison. `GenPlainSub`, `describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T)` beside `describe(x: Circle)`, prints `circle, generic, circle` in either order (`ProjectFortress/tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss`), as the compiled run does. When the chosen generic declaration's instance, made by rung K's inference and answer 8's promotion, converts an argument, the call converts and dispatches again through the overloaded function (`convertedCall`, `:1222-1239`), so `opz(z, w)` with a `ZZ32` and a `ZZ64` runs `opz(a: ZZ64, b: ZZ64)` (`ProjectFortress/tests/DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`); not for overloaded methods. The shared symbolic instantiation of generic functions and constructors is keyed by each static parameter's kind and bounds as well as its name (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:57-68`), so two overloads whose parameters share a name keep their own bounds (row 478, `ProjectFortress/tests/GenericOverloadBoundsApart.fss`); a `where` clause is still not in the key (the team's TODO, `FGenericFunction.java:49-51`).

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § Execution model: added at climb batch 7b's gather (rung W); rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains, and covers an overlap through `comprises` clauses, where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses** (2026-09-29, climb batch 7b rung W, `8f7e183d4`; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 and 5.4; the conversion decision of POSITIONS 2026-09-28, item 4; item 26, POSITIONS 2026-09-29). Both run only where today's check refuses (`OverloadedFunction.java:494-497`), so no set that loaded before is refused. For one own generic beside a plain declaration (`validOnDeclaredDomains`, `:692-721`): equal declared domains stay refused; one inside the other is valid when the inner one's return type is below the outer one's with the generic's type parameters standing for themselves, which is sound for every instance and refuses the Types paper's `baz` pair (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXGenericBesidePlainReturnRule.fss`); neither inside the other is valid when plain declarations below both cover the overlap, the generic read at its bounds and only when each type parameter is a whole parameter type with at most one bound naming no static parameter. For two plain declarations with an unrelated parameter pair (`overlapCovered`, `:799-808`), the overlap is distributed over the `comprises` clauses, excluding pairs dropped (`overlapPieces`, `:901-945`), and every combination of its parts must lie inside one declaration below both. The search refuses on a cycle, after 10,000 steps or 4,096 combinations, on a symbolic type, or when the clauses do not settle. The helpers are private to the load check; `FType.meet` and subtyping are unchanged. Pairs of two generic declarations keep today's check (Q4 = (1)), so row 159's renamed and swapped pairs stay refused. Loaded now: `O2Z64`, `O2Meet`, the Meet Rule's `comprises` example (`ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss`), `MeetViaExclusion`, the proof addendum's `CoverageReturnGood` in both orders (`ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesCoverReturn.fss`), `BetweenTwoClosed` (`f(g) = 3`). Still refused: `MeetViaExclusionNoV` (`XXXComprisesMeetUncovered`), `CoverageReturnBad`, now on the return-type rule (`XXXComprisesCoverReturnWrong`), a generic declaration with two bounds beside the plain declarations that cover its overlap (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXGenericBesidePlainTwoBounds.fss`, row 552), and the POPL 2019 paper's `ArrayList`/`List` set of three generic declarations (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk.fss`, row 539). Walk checks no `comprises` clause's closure, so an object that extends two closed traits unlisted loads beside a covered set and runs the first-written of two incomparable declarations (row 551).

### The checker and the one library

- **The compiled checker's exclusion rule is the designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion", relaxing it alone is unsound, and the real fork is the code generator's dispatch of generics** (2026-09-22: rung P of batch 3 stopped, `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-relax/REPORT.md`, taken into the tree at the batch's gather; `reviews/multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md`; `reviews/mie-probes/dispatch-and-route-c.md`). Since climb batch 7b's rung L (`070ef39e5`), `TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax[\TotalComparison\]` beside `Comparison` (item 22, (b); `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:120-122`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:158-160`), so the sentence below that it extends `Comparison` alone is climb batch 7's state. The rule "forbids multiple instantiation inheritance, in which a type is a subtype of distinct applications of a type constructor" (`Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152`; Naden 2012, `Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497`, who records that it conflicts with the numeric tower and leaves that open, `:568-632`); it entered the checker 2010-05-28 (`5a6b7913b`) and became `checkP` 2010-07-26 (`e828b44b1`); the nested tower is 2008. The compiled checker enforces it in the two hierarchy questions and relies on it in the return-type rule (`OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105`); with it relaxed under any placement, `ProbeMIEPick.fss` type-checks and dies with `IncompatibleClassChangeError`. The interpreter has no such clause, dispatches a generic on a double-member object by the first-listed instantiation (`FType.java:568-574`), refuses overloads lacking an excluding pair, and dies at run time on other shapes. Pavol chose route A, keep the rule and flatten the tower (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, the exclusion route, rung P's fork), and it is built: the interpreter converts by coercion (climb batch 4 rung C), the specification states the rule (climb batch 5 rung S) and the number tower is flat (climb batch 6 rung F). The routes not taken were dropping the rule (22 lines, 93 → 33 then, with the dispatcher changed to take the call site's static arguments, since sized at 43 lines in "The exclusion fork, priced three ways and dated" below) and a per-trait guard (28 lines, refusing 69 library pairs, the tower's own implementations). On the nested tower the rule bit 61 errors at 23 library declarations (13 tower, 4 comparisons, 4 `Maybe`, 2 reductions), and on the flat library 18, at the comparison and `Maybe` families and at `RelationalPredicateCondition`; climb batch 7's rung H (`952892a00`; `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/REPORT.md` sections 4 to 9) brought the library to the rule, and the checker reports no exclusion error on it (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-7/gate/distance.txt:3`): `TotalComparison` extends `Comparison` alone, as the compiler prelude's does (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:719-722`), and extends no order, as the specification's does, whose supertypes are `Comparison` and the three traits of `LEXICO`'s algebra (`Specification/advanced-lib/comparison.tex:28-32`), restating `>=`, `<=`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX` at itself with `StandardTotalOrder`'s bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:170-175`); `AnyMaybe` extends `AnyUniqueItem` alone and writes the `opr =` its api declares (`.fss:1400-1403`); `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` no longer excludes its own supertype, its component-only second `ANDCOND` renamed `andRelCond` and chosen by a `typecase` in `andCondCombine` at `FilterGenerator2`'s two call sites (`.fss:4523`, `:4525`, `:4565-4575`), zero.md's P3d with the two changes the compiled checker needs. The cost: a program's own `p1 ANDCOND p2` of two relational predicates is no longer relational under walk, while `filter` keeps the fusion (row 458). Dispatch, measured: a static argument is a constant in the loaded class's name only when no dispatch is needed; a dispatched generic arm reads it from the run-time value, which records only its last-listed instantiation (`OverloadSet.java:1411-1696`, `STypesUtil.scala:1276`). `MieDispatchSub` (generic overloads on `Tag[\X\]` and on its subtrait `Sub[\X\]`, called with an object that extends `Sub[\Red\]` and `Tag[\Blue\]` and so is a double member of `Tag`) is refused by today's checker with four hierarchy errors (`reviews/mie-probes/MieDispatchSub.compiled.txt:1-11`); with the rule relaxed it compiles and throws `ClassCastException` (`:12-18`). Two defects need no double membership: a generic arm reached through a less specific declaration throws whenever its return type mentions its parameter (`reviews/mie-probes/scope/ScopeAlpha2.compiled.txt:1-6`), and a run-time-made `ZZ32` instantiation is named differently from the static one (`scope/ScopeZZ32Sub.compiled.txt:1-6`); both programs are legal under route A, type-check on today's checker and die with `ClassCastException`, and the 43-line call-site change fixes both inside template dispatchers only (`scope-call-site-dispatch.md` § 4). And the overloading checker never examines symbolic operators (`OverloadingChecker.scala:546-550`). None of the three has a ledger row (`reviews/batch-3-conformance.md`, rung P).

### The harness and the gate

<!-- moved 2026-09-30 from FACTS.md § The harness and the gate: added at climb batch 7b's gather (rung C); rewritten timeless under the same title -->
- **A harness run against another build's classes must point `FORTRESS_CACHES` at that build's caches as well as passing `-Dfortress.caches`** (2026-09-30, climb batch 7b rung C, `e2f1aa7e8`). A `run` step of a `.test` file is a separate process, `bin/fortress run <name>` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:470-500`), whose class path `bin/run_classpath` builds from `FORTRESS_CACHES` or `default_repository/caches`; without it the run step of a program compiled into another cache fails "Could not load ... Resource not found". The run step executes no checker code, so the tree's own classes serve it.

### Execution model

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (`compile-ladder/rung-export-var/`). `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it — a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" — and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only. A declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. So a comment-only edit to the library is not neutral at the syntax-tree level: the library's comment-only edit widened three spans (the scalar block's first `-` in both files, `SUFFIX_SUM` in the `.fsi`), besides shifting every position below each insertion, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics must map positions back first (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/parse-compare.sh`, `ast-compare.py`, `remap-lines.py`). No answer changed.

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees** (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, section 4.1): `throw new FortressError((FObject) Driver.getFortressLibrary().getRootValue(name))` from inside a `builtinPrimitive` method reaches `Evaluator.forTry` unchanged (`MethodClosure.java:85-86` has no `catch`) and matches `catch e IntegerOverflow`; `Int.overflow()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:258-261`) is the helper and `WellKnownNames.integerOverflowException` the name. Measured by the 25 `overflows(...)` assertions of `ProjectFortress/tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, whose helper catches nothing but `IntegerOverflow`. The natives that raise it: the shift, `GCD` and `LCM` natives of the integer rules ("The interpreter's integer rules" under Landed semantics), the eighteen fixed-width arithmetic natives, `^` and `CHOOSE` on the four fixed widths, `LCM` on `NN32` and `NN64`, and the narrowing checks `Int.rc` and `NN32.rc` (row 347 closed; "Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" under Landed semantics). The interpreter's mapping of every other Java exception is unchanged (`FunctionClosure.java:188-196`), so row 336's division by zero still ends the run.

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The compiled run's class loader takes its first load of a name under the JDK's class-loading lock, and a generic arm's first load is safe on four threads** (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1, 11, 12; row 417). `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` runs under `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, as the JDK's own `ClassLoader.loadClass` does (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/jdk-loadclass-javap.txt:2-9`). No loader in the tree registers as parallel-capable, so that lock is the loader's own monitor, the one the JVM already holds when it resolves a class through the loader. The explicit loads, `RTHelpers.loadClosureClass`, `RTHelpers.getRTTIclass` and the union instantiation, are under it too. `history` is still written before `defineClass`, safe under the lock. Measured: `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG` fails 5 of 5 compiled runs at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` without the lock and passes 5 of 5 with it (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/threads-before.txt:10-14`, `threads-after.txt:10-14`). The gate's four-thread stage runs it as its fourteenth program. Cost: none measurable; against a loader without the lock, seven interleaved runs each at four threads, the medians differ by -42 to +62 ms on the thirteen `atomic` programs, whose runs take 270 to 1,400 ms (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/lock-cost.txt`; nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, load 4.2 to 5.1, JDK 25).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains, so the order they are written in no longer decides** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 5.1; POSITIONS, "The static-parameter sentence goes"; row 548). `OverloadedFunction.bestMatchInternal` keeps a candidate by `moreSpecificDeclaration` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:1335-1342`). When one of two applicable declarations is a generic function or constructor with static parameters of its own, their declared domains are compared: the symbolic instantiation, each type parameter standing for itself with its bounds as supertypes, and a domain lies inside a generic one when walk's inference finds an instance holding it from values that carry only its types (`instanceHolding`, `:1291-1306`). Otherwise, as for two plain declarations, their instances' domains are compared. A functional method of a generic trait and a generic dotted method keep the instance comparison. `GenPlainSub`, `describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T)` beside `describe(x: Circle)`, prints `circle, generic, circle` in either order (`ProjectFortress/tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss`), as the compiled run does. When the chosen generic declaration's instance, made by walk's inference with coercion and answer 8's promotion ("Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion ..." under Landed semantics), converts an argument, the call converts and dispatches again through the overloaded function (`convertedCall`, `:1222-1239`), so `opz(z, w)` with a `ZZ32` and a `ZZ64` runs `opz(a: ZZ64, b: ZZ64)` (`ProjectFortress/tests/DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`); not for overloaded methods. The shared symbolic instantiation of generic functions and constructors is keyed by each static parameter's kind and bounds as well as its name (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:57-68`), so two overloads whose parameters share a name keep their own bounds (row 478, fixed; `ProjectFortress/tests/GenericOverloadBoundsApart.fss`); a `where` clause is not in the key (the team's TODO, `FGenericFunction.java:49-51`).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Execution model: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains, and covers an overlap through `comprises` clauses, where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses** (`compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 and 5.4; POSITIONS, "Conversions never change which declaration runs" and "The `comprises` passages read at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491)"; row 492, fixed). Both run only where the parameter-by-parameter check refuses (`OverloadedFunction.java:494-497`), so they refuse no set that check loads. For one own generic beside a plain declaration (`validOnDeclaredDomains`, `:692-721`): equal declared domains are refused; one inside the other is valid when the inner one's return type is below the outer one's with the generic's type parameters standing for themselves, which is sound for every instance and refuses the Types paper's `baz` pair (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXGenericBesidePlainReturnRule.fss`); neither inside the other is valid when plain declarations below both cover the overlap, the generic read at its bounds and only when each type parameter is a whole parameter type with at most one bound naming no static parameter. For two plain declarations with an unrelated parameter pair (`overlapCovered`, `:799-808`), the overlap is distributed over the `comprises` clauses, excluding pairs dropped (`overlapPieces`, `:901-945`), and every combination of its parts must lie inside one declaration below both. The search refuses on a cycle, after 10,000 steps or 4,096 combinations, on a symbolic type, or when the clauses do not settle. The helpers are private to the load check; `FType.meet` and subtyping do not use them. Pairs of two generic declarations take the parameter-by-parameter check alone (Q4 = (1)), so row 159's renamed and swapped pairs are refused. Loaded: `O2Z64`, `O2Meet`, the Meet Rule's `comprises` example (`ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss`), `MeetViaExclusion`, the proof addendum's `CoverageReturnGood` in both orders (`ProjectFortress/tests/ComprisesCoverReturn.fss`), `BetweenTwoClosed` (`f(g) = 3`). Refused: `MeetViaExclusionNoV` (`XXXComprisesMeetUncovered`), `CoverageReturnBad`, on the return-type rule (`XXXComprisesCoverReturnWrong`), a generic declaration with two bounds beside the plain declarations that cover its overlap (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXGenericBesidePlainTwoBounds.fss`, row 552), and the POPL 2019 paper's `ArrayList`/`List` set of three generic declarations (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk.fss`, row 539). Walk checks no `comprises` clause's closure, so an object that extends two closed traits unlisted loads beside a covered set and runs the first-written of two incomparable declarations (row 551).

### The checker and the one library

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The compiled checker's exclusion rule is the designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion", relaxing it alone is unsound, and the real fork is the code generator's dispatch of generics** (`compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-relax/REPORT.md`; `reviews/multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md`; `reviews/mie-probes/dispatch-and-route-c.md`). The rule "forbids multiple instantiation inheritance, in which a type is a subtype of distinct applications of a type constructor" (`Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152`; Naden 2012, `Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497`, who records that it conflicts with the numeric tower and leaves that open, `:568-632`); it entered the checker in `5a6b7913b` and became `checkP` in `e828b44b1`, two years after the nested tower. The compiled checker enforces it in the two hierarchy questions and relies on it in the return-type rule (`OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105`); with it relaxed under any placement, `ProbeMIEPick.fss` type-checks and dies with `IncompatibleClassChangeError`. The interpreter has no such clause, dispatches a generic on a double-member object by the first-listed instantiation (`FType.java:568-574`), refuses overloads lacking an excluding pair, and dies at run time on other shapes. Route A, keep the rule and flatten the tower, is built (POSITIONS, "The exclusion rule stays and the tower is flat"): the interpreter converts by coercion, the specification states the rule and the number tower is flat (the entries under Landed semantics and The specification). The library is brought to the rule, and the checker reports no exclusion error on it (`compile-ladder/gate/`'s `distance.txt`, exclusion 0): `TotalComparison` extends `Comparison` and `StandardMinMax[\TotalComparison\]`, and no order (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:120-122`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:158-160`; POSITIONS, "Appendix I's small items"; row 461), where the compiler prelude's extends `Comparison` alone (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:719-722`) and the specification's has as supertypes `Comparison` and the three traits of `LEXICO`'s algebra (`Specification/advanced-lib/comparison.tex:28-32`); it restates `>=`, `<=`, `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX` at itself with `StandardTotalOrder`'s bodies (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:170-175`), so generic code bounded by `StandardMin` or `StandardMax` takes total comparisons; `AnyMaybe` extends `AnyUniqueItem` alone and writes the `opr =` its api declares (`.fss:1400-1403`); `RelationalPredicateCondition[\E\]` no longer excludes its own supertype, its component-only second `ANDCOND` renamed `andRelCond` and chosen by a `typecase` in `andCondCombine` at `FilterGenerator2`'s two call sites (`.fss:4523`, `:4525`, `:4565-4575`). The cost: a program's own `p1 ANDCOND p2` of two relational predicates is no longer relational under walk, while `filter` keeps the fusion (row 458). Dispatch, measured: a static argument is a constant in the loaded class's name only when no dispatch is needed; a dispatched generic arm reads it from the run-time value, which records only its last-listed instantiation (`OverloadSet.java:1411-1696`, `STypesUtil.scala:1276`). `MieDispatchSub` (generic overloads on `Tag[\X\]` and on its subtrait `Sub[\X\]`, called with an object that extends `Sub[\Red\]` and `Tag[\Blue\]` and so is a double member of `Tag`) is refused by the checker with four hierarchy errors (`reviews/mie-probes/MieDispatchSub.compiled.txt:1-11`); with the rule relaxed it compiles and throws `ClassCastException` (`:12-18`). Two defects need no double membership: a generic arm reached through a less specific declaration threw whenever its return type mentioned its parameter (`reviews/mie-probes/scope/ScopeAlpha2.compiled.txt:1-6`), and a run-time-made `ZZ32` instantiation was named differently from the static one (`scope/ScopeZZ32Sub.compiled.txt:1-6`); both are fixed inside template dispatchers ("A generic arm of a template dispatcher is called at the dispatcher's own static parameters" under Landed semantics) and stand for generic dotted methods and non-template dispatchers (rows 495, 496). And the overloading checker never examines symbolic operators (`OverloadingChecker.scala:546-550`), with no ledger row (`reviews/batch-3-conformance.md`, rung P).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters** (`compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md`). A size is a symbol or a literal compared by equality; an unknown one is an inference variable of its own, a syntax-tree node `_InferenceVarInt` beside the two the checker had (30 regenerated node files, 26 changed and 4 new, deterministic), with a third constraint track in `Formula`; `keep-size-params` in `TypeSchemaAnalyzer`; kind-correct static arguments in `AbstractMethodChecker` and `FnNameInfo.boundsFor`; the export checker compares sizes (`ExportChecker.equalIntExprs` was the constant `false`), so a component that exports its own sized api checks (`compiler_tests/NatExportChecker`); arithmetic in a size, and inference of a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` parameter, refused by name. A size left unknown in a call's static arguments is refused at the call, "Could not infer static argument ... without context": this is Pavol's rule for sizes (POSITIONS, "Sizes"), and it is stricter than the types' rule, under which a dead type parameter becomes `BOTTOM` and the call compiles (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1937-1940`; `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/dead-type-single.txt`). In an overload set the call is refused when such an arm is the most specific, unless its unknown size occurs in its own parameter type ("The compiled checker refuses a call whose most specific arm has a size the call cannot fix" below). Inferred, written-out, method-on-sized-receiver and several-sizes-at-one-call programs check (`compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, whose `dot` solves three sizes at one call, one shared by both arguments; `NatWrittenChecker`; `NatMethodChecker`); a mismatch is refused (`XXXNatMismatchChecker`). What the checker left, a sized program failing at load (`3$RTTIc`), code generation refusing a sized overload set (`OverloadSet.java:1199`) and a size in `extends` (`CodeGen.java:5793`), is built as the run-time descriptor, and the three expected failures that gated them are the plain tests `NatArgRungS`, `NatDispArmChecker` and `NatOverrideChecker` ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § The checker and the one library: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion and answer 8's promotion, keeps the expected type at a call written `f(x)`, ranks every declaration applicable only with coercion together, generic or not, and refuses a tie among them unless it is a numeral's** (`compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md`). **The attempts.** A call's candidates are tried by subtyping with the expected type; failing that with coercion; failing that both again without it. The first attempt is by subtyping under the expected type and counts only candidates without a coercion the call needs; a declaration that fits the call's arguments but whose result the expected type refuses is not among its candidates. So when none fits under the expected type, the attempt with coercion ranks every declaration applicable with coercion (the coercion chapter's Σ′), and a declaration reached by coercion whose result fits can win over one that fits the arguments as they are: `a: V = k(NOf(1))`, with `k[\T extends N\](x: T): T` beside `k(x: V): V` and `V` coercing from `N`, runs `k(V)`, where walk runs the generic; the reserved stop "a ranking that lets a declaration needing a conversion win over one that fits the call as it is" was met and listed (row 508, gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXInferContextKeepsFit`; its repair is decided, POSITIONS, "The order of the checker's attempts at a call", batch 8). An attempt is kept only when its most specific candidate's result converts to the expected type. A call no attempt keeps takes the first attempt holding a candidate: for a call written `f(x)`, among the attempts without the context, so that the binding reports a call the rule accepts; for any other call, among those with it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:604-752`; `Operators.scala:85`, `:90`, `:197`, `:345`). **The coercion attempt** (`checkApplicableWithCoercion`, `Functionals.scala:280-400`). A type parameter that is a position's whole type takes the narrowest type, under the coercion chapter's no-less-specific relation, among its arguments' types, the types they coerce to and its bound. The types they coerce to come from a lookup from a source to its coercion targets (`CoercionOracle.getCoercionTargetsFrom`, over `TraitTable.coercingTraits`). Structured positions and the expected type constrain the solver by subtyping. Every argument is then admitted by subtyping or coercion. It refuses a call with an untyped function argument and one with more than 64 combinations of chosen types (rows 507 and 506). **The promotion.** A candidate that subtyping instantiates with a union is instantiated again at the narrowest named type (`pick(z, l)`: `ZZ64`, `z` converted). **The ranking.** A candidate with a counted coercion ranks below one without; a promoted candidate's coercions are not counted. A promoted candidate, and a generic one of the coercion attempt, are compared on their declared domains by the overloading oracle's subtyping, strictly one way; between two converted candidates it decides when it relates them one way, and the coercion chapter's order on the instances decides otherwise (`useful/STypesUtil.scala:1064-1113`; `CoercionOracle.scala:76-84`). **The head and the tie.** The head is the specification's maximal element. A tie among candidates with counted coercions is refused, "Ambiguous coercion in call to function f: ...", a generic declaration listed by its declared domain. The exception is a tie differing only where the argument is a numeral: the numeral is read as `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by a literal's magnitude (a size used as a value as `ZZ32`), and the call resolves as an argument of that type would, over every candidate, those the reading fits without coercion first (`pickb(3000000000)` beside `pickb(NN32)`, `pickb(ZZ32)` and `pickb(ZZ64)` takes `pickb(ZZ64)`). ### The harness and the gate

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § The harness and the gate: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The `XXX` expected-failure mechanism in `compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` can express a compile-stage failure only, and a run-time defect needs two `.test` files** (`compile-ladder/rung-tryatomic/`). `shouldFail` comes from the `.test` file name (`FileTests.java:932`) and the same flag reaches every stage the file drives (`:1052-1059`, `:1063-1069`), so an `XXX` file that carries `link` or `compile` demands that the compile fail (`:384-404`, message at `:402`); and a `TestTest` fails on an unsatisfied `run_out_*` verdict whatever `shouldFail` says (`:534-539`, `:583-585`), with `pass`/`PASS` demanded by default when no check is set (`:276-282`). A compiles-but-crashes defect is therefore gated as two `.test` files over one component — a plain-named one driving `link`, an `XXX`-named one driving `run` with a marker the failing run does print — shown going red on a deliberate fix (`compile-ladder/rung-tryatomic/raw/junit-xxx-expected.txt`, `raw/junit-xxx-goes-red.txt`). Run together in one JVM, as a repair's new tests are (`junit.sh`'s `ONE_JVM=1` mode, `compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh`; `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 6), `Shell junit` hands the list to `FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:1086`), which puts the compile and link tests in the suite before the run tests (`FileTests.java:997-1004`), so a pair's link test runs before its `XXX` run test.

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § The harness and the gate: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->

There the expected-failure branch keys on `f.contains("XXX")` (`:346`) with `f = join(_dir, _name)` (`:82`) and `_name` the `.test` file's `tests=` value (`:1052-1059`) — **not** the `.test` file name of `:932` that the printed-error files use through `:384-404`, so the `XXX` prefix must be on the component name. The check stream on that path is the harness's third one, `"exception"` (`:136`), whose contents are `ex.toString()` (`:344-345`), prefixed by the command at `:702-704`, so the key is `compile_exception_contains`. When the compile throws instead, the harness checks an `exception` key against the exception's `toString()`, and a met key prints " OK Saw expected exception", not "Saw expected failure" (`FileTests.java:341-361`; `compile-ladder/rung-unknown-size-arm/probes/repair-tests.txt`).

- **A harness run against another build's classes must point `FORTRESS_CACHES` at that build's caches as well as passing `-Dfortress.caches`** (`compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/REPORT.md` section 4). A `run` step of a `.test` file is a separate process, `bin/fortress run <name>` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:470-500`), whose class path `bin/run_classpath` builds from `FORTRESS_CACHES` or `default_repository/caches`; without it the run step of a program compiled into another cache fails "Could not load ... Resource not found". The run step executes no checker code, so the tree's own classes serve it.

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Landed semantics: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- The compiled world's mutable-variable cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the language's top type, not `runtimeValues.FValue`: `FValue` is an abstract class (`runtimeValues/FValue.java:13`) and a compiled closure is not one of its subclasses, so a mutable variable of arrow type failed the verifier. The defect was in the tree for *local* mutable variables too, which have always been stored in such a cell (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P15LocalArrow.fss`, `P16LocalArrowTask.fss`: `VerifyError` before, `f(1) = 3` after), and both kinds are fixed by widening the payload (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:18-32`, `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:20,27-28,144,152,226`).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Landed semantics: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:397-399,427-430` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).

<!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Landed semantics: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **The repair turns one loud failure into a quiet value, and the value it prints is wrong even though the value it holds is right.** `FIntLiteral.asNN64` threw for every string-carried numeral before the repair above, and `simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger` sends every `IntLiteral` arithmetic result of bit length 64 or more to the string branch (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntLiteralArith.java:31-32`), a path the repair does not touch — so the transition needs no numeral of bit length 64 in the source at all. `x = 9223372036854775807` then `n: NN64 = x + x + 1` raised `Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615` before and computes $2^{64}-1$ now, which `literals.tex:83-86` makes the correct value, and prints it as `-1` because `FNN64.toString` is signed (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20`, ledger row 326, open). The probe is `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/skeptic/s3.fss` with `s3.compiled` and `s3.walk`; `walk` refuses the coercion instead ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type NN64"). The error that named the true value is gone while the rendering is wrong, so row 326 and this fact are one situation and should be read together.

- The interpreter's integer rules: fixed-width `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `|..|`, `DIV` and multiplication raise a catchable `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit ("Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" below); `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` and `NN64` saturate at the width and reverse on a negative count, the count read by the class of its value (an `NN64` count of `2^63` or more is beyond the width, a `ZZ` count is read exactly); the unbounded `ZZ`'s shift count is exact at any size, a negative one giving `0` or `-1` and an unrepresentable left shift a catchable `IntegerOverflow`, refused before the JVM allocates it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/BigNum.java:247`); `GCD` and `LCM` on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` are nonnegative and an unrepresentable result, `MIN GCD 0` and `MIN GCD MIN` included, is a catchable `IntegerOverflow`; `LCM` on the unbounded `ZZ` is nonnegative (`BigNum.java:176-192`); `0 LCM 0` is `0` on all five integer types (row 385); `LCM` on `NN32` and `NN64`, `CHOOSE` and `^` on the four fixed widths raise a catchable `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit, and `CHOOSE` answers 0 for `k<0` or `k>n` (`tests/PowChooseLcmRungE.fss`; row 337); `ZZ64.narrow` keeps the low 32 bits; the specification's `shift` is declared on `ZZ` (next entry) and absent from the compiler prelude (row 383, expected failure `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXShiftDeclRungI.test`). <!-- moved 2026-10-02 from FACTS.md § Landed semantics: shortened in place under the same title to the fact, its source and its test -->
- **Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check** (`compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/REPORT.md`; for generic declarations `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md`): a single function's, constructor's, method's or native's parameter (`NonPrimitive.typecheckParams` and the generic unification path), a generic function's parameter of a declared type among them (row 388, `ProjectFortress/tests/CoercionGenericFnRungC.fss`); an overloaded call when no overload applies without coercion (`OverloadedFunction.bestMatchWithCoercion`, at the team's "TODO add checks for COERCE, right here." of `OverloadedFunction.java:792` as the team left it), generic declarations among the candidates, each instantiated by walk's inference with coercion ("Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion ..." below), the most specific chosen by `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:477-484` and a call with no most specific refused as "Ambiguous coercion"; and a typed binding or assignment (`LHSEvaluator`, `BaseEnv`, `BuildEnvironments`, `LazilyEvaluatedCell`), where a variable, field or parameter declared with a tuple type converts element by element and an element already of its type is kept (`:708-719`). The conversions are the disambiguator's lifted `coerce_` functions, found at the declared type's top level and chosen on the run-time value, a generic trait's coercion whose static parameters are the trait's own instantiated with the target's static arguments (row 389, `ProjectFortress/tests/CoercionGenericTraitRungC.fss`); the converted arguments of an overloaded call are dispatched as an ordinary call, so the declaration that runs is the most specific for the converted value's run-time type (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:73-78`, `:466-468`; `ProjectFortress/tests/CoercionRedispatchRungC.fss`). An overloaded function keeps the coercions per argument types in its cache (`OverloadedFunction.java:760-776`) and re-dispatches every converted call; an overloaded method caches nothing (`OverloadedMethod.mcache` is declared at `OverloadedMethod.java:28`, read at `:48` and `:56`, and written nowhere). Route A's price, in its general form: an argument whose static type needs a coercion while its run-time type plainly matches another overload dispatches plainly under `walk`, where the compiled run and the specification apply the coercion (`conversions-coercions.tex:525-536`, `:567-570`); gated as two expected failures, `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionStaticRungC.fss` (the specification's example, 4 under `walk` against 3) and `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC.fss` (`g(NarrowOf)` under `walk` against `g(Wide)` compiled, `compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/probes/skeptic/diff-1.txt:255`, `:263`); accepted as the interpreter's limit until after the switch-over (POSITIONS, "Walk chooses coercions on the value, for now"). Not converted, each gated as an expected failure: a declared return type (row 387), a generic trait's coercion that declares its own static parameter (row 513, `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionOwnStaticRungK.fss`), an overloaded function's tuple-typed parameter or an assignment to a tuple-typed field (395); varargs, keyword and arrow targets are not converted and not measured. Three interpreter tests print differently under it and nothing converts in any of them: `XXXimmutableTopLevel`, the Java line numbers of a printed stack trace through `LazilyEvaluatedCell.java` and `BaseEnv.java`, and `taskTrace2` and `taskTrace3`, identity hash codes (`Evaluator@hex`); all three are identical once those are normalised (`compile-ladder/rung-interp-coercion/probes/stay-green-repair.txt`), which is what the gate's masks cover (POSITIONS, "The gate's comparisons").

- **A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`, and a sized program loads, dispatches and runs compiled** (`compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/REPORT.md`; rows 307, 402). One `RTTIsize` per number, made from its text by `RTTIsize.of` (a `ConcurrentHashMap`, get then `putIfAbsent` returning the winner, the team's factory pattern of `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:2744-2752`), hashing on its text, a supertype only of an equal size; the loader's `MethodInstantiater.rttiReference`, the `extends`-clause push and the dispatcher's literal leaf call it (design B with the factory, POSITIONS, "The run-time size design is B"). A size symbol in an arm's parameter type is read off the value's descriptor as a type variable is, and `DOT`'s shared size needs only the team's second-occurrence check. A size read as a value is one `CONST.Nat` call that the loader replaces by the `IntLiteral` of the instantiated numeral, through `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr`'s int, long or String branch (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:225-241`), so it reads back exactly; a size is at most 4294967295 (`nat`) or within `ZZ32` (`int`), refused beyond ("A size beyond `NN32` or `ZZ32` is refused on both paths" below), and `compiler_tests/NatRtBigSize` gates 2^31-1 to 2^32-1; a size symbol as a generic method's static argument is substituted at load (`CodeGen.isSymbolic`). A size is read as a value, captured and used to instantiate in a loop body, a comprehension, a `fn` expression, nested closures and an object's method (`compiler_tests/NatRtClosure`) and a trait's default method (`compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/probes/differential-repair-own.txt:84-106`) as elsewhere, because `FreeVarTypes` counts it as a closure's free static parameter, and in a parallel task too ("A parallel task in a generic declaration is generic over its free static parameters" below; rows 419, 420). Gated by 17 `compiler_tests/NatRt*` and the promoted `NatArgRungS`, `NatDispArmChecker` and `NatOverrideChecker`; walk and the compiled run agree on all of them at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` and `4`, `NatRtBigSize` included (row 418, closed). `RTTI`'s serial-number counter is atomic: sizes made on eight threads at once had shared a serial number 7,638 times in ten rounds, and the closure loader keys a generic arm's closure on them (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/RTHelpers.java:160-170`; row 415). The checker's instantiation exclusion counts two different literal sizes (row 402), and only literals: a size symbol against a literal is not known to differ, as a type variable against a type is not (`compiler_tests/XXXNatAmbigChecker` gates the ambiguous pair a first form accepted). The literal leaf's table lookup costs at most a few nanoseconds on a dispatched call of about 23 ns: 0.9 ns on one build and 2.6 ns on another, each the median over rounds 3 and 4 of three runs of the literal-size arm's dispatched-minus-static time less the no-size arm's, six values from -2.2 to 7.0 ns (`compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/probes/lookup-cost.txt`; nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, load at start 4.2 to 5.9, JDK 25, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`); the static-field remedy is not built. No library declaration is refused by it. Open: a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic constructor (row 408), the `extends Object` bound on a size (row 412), a dispatched arm with a concrete generic bound (row 413), the declaration rule with a static-parameter argument (row 414) and walk's missing instantiation exclusion in overloading (row 416).

Mixed without parentheses with `+`, `BITAND` or each other across the ⨰ boundary they are refused before evaluation, as `Specification/appendices/operators.tex:27-29` requires; ∔ and ∸ mix left-associatively and ⨰ binds tighter (`:191`, `:213-224`). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/WrapOperatorsRungD.fss` (36 assertions).

- **The one library's number tower is flat** (`compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/`; rows 146, 423, 428). `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR64` and `RR32` are siblings under `Number` (`Number comprises { RR64, RR32, QQ, AnyIntegral }`, `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ, ZZ64, ZZ32, NN64, NN32 }`; "`RR32` is a sibling of `RR64` under `Number`, and `RR64` converts from it" below), each carrying its own algebra: `RR64` and `QQ` extend `StandardPartialOrder`, `StandardMinMax`, `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing` at their own type, and `Integral[\I\]` extends `StandardTotalOrder[\I\]`, `MultiplicativeRing[\I\]` and `AnyIntegral` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:281-611`; `NN32` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi`). Each wider type declares `coerce` from each narrower one, exactly answer 8's table: `ZZ64` from `ZZ32` and `NN32`; `NN64` from `NN32`; `ZZ` from the four fixed widths; `QQ` from all five integer types; `RR64` from `ZZ32` (and so from every numeral that fits it) and from `RR32`, and from nothing else (`NN32` into `RR64` is decided and not yet built, POSITIONS, "`NN32` coerces into `RR64`"). `Number` declares only `asFloat(self): RR64` (in the api too) and one numeric `opr =`: two exact numbers compare as rationals, which is what `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:369-370` says of rationals; a float and any number compare after `asFloat`, so an exact value equals its nearest float and the relation is not transitive (`1/3 = asFloat(1/3)` is `true`; `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/probes/skeptic/sk-exprs-equality.txt:19-26`), on which the specification is silent (row 434). `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ` and `QQ` reach `RR64` only by an explicit `asFloat`; integer `/` always answers a `Ratio`, which prints without `/1`. `SUM` and `PROD` are generic reductions over `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` whose identity comes from the static argument through a `() -> T` witness `typecase` over the eight number leaves, narrowest first; a clause form whose element type no argument fixes writes it (`SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#i] ...`), and an unwritten one fails under `walk`, empty with `CastError`, nonempty with a join unification error (row 424). `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `BIG MINMAXN` are gone. `QQ`'s arithmetic is exact, its parts always `BigNum`s (row 428); a `ZZ64` bound to a numeral holds 64 bits (row 146). Under `walk`, a bare big operator over a list literal of numerals is refused (row 432), and a `ZZ32` scalar meets an `RR64` array or matrix in a generic operator by conversion, the container fixing `T` at `RR64` (row 388, closed; `ProjectFortress/tests/InferCoercionRungK.fss:59-67`). Gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/FlatTowerRungF.fss`; by `RR32MixedRungF.fss` (`RR32` plus an `RR64`, row 435, closed); and by two expected failures that assert the specification's answer where `walk` on the flat library does not give it: `XXXUnwrittenSumRungF.fss` (an unwritten clause-form `SUM` or `PROD`, row 424) and `XXXEmptyGroupSumRungF.fss` (an empty `SUM` over a non-number additive group, row 436). The two microGPT checks pass 40 of 40 with the same printed values as on the nested tower; 89 team-test lines were respelled for the flat tower, each keeping the value the test checks.

- **A typecase or catch clause's bound name is a local on the compiled path, so the compiled `cast[\T\]` matches a value of type `T`** (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md`; rows 351, 426). `CodeGen.forTypecase` binds a named clause's matched value, cast to the clause's type, as a local of a nested scope for the clause body, the shape of `forLocalVarDecl`. `CodeGen.forTry` binds the catch name to the exception's value the same way. A clause without a name is generated as before. The compiler library's `cast` template stores and reads its `y` where it had read a missing top-level object; that template is the one class of the five library jars that changed (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/library-jars.txt`, `cast-template-javap.txt`). What it does not reach: `cast[\ZZ32\](0)` still throws, because a numeral is not a `ZZ32` (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-141`). A name bound inside a clause's pattern, which the coercion desugarer produces and a program may write (`Leaf(i) => i`; the team's ungated `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/patternMatching1.fss:37-43`), is still unbound on the compiled path, and walk refuses it too (rows 340, 498; `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/skeptic/pattern-bind.txt:6`, `:17`, `:27`). A named clause or a `catch` inside a `do … also` arm whose body then reads a captured variable still fails verification: a local in a task body takes `this`'s slot (row 497), and a `catch` there also meets row 322's mechanism (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/skeptic/clause-in-task.txt:33-34`, `:50`, `clause-in-task-split.txt:62`, `:95`, `try-in-arm.txt:41`). Gated by `compiler_tests/TypecaseBindRungG`, `CastBindRungG`, `ArrowClauseBindRungG` (`andCondCombine`'s shape: a binding at an arrow over the function's own type parameter, nested), `WitnessIdentityRungG` and `library_tests/ClauseBindingRungB`.

Row 420 was the same defect: the generic method's `||` operands are run as a task, and a one-parameter method with two task operands failed the same way (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/row420-cause-before.txt`). It tests the arm so read with a plain `instanceof` and calls it by name, and the loader sets both to the call site's arguments. This is the measured 43-line change without its probe switch. It fixes a generic arm that names its parameters differently (`compiler_tests/DispatchRenamedArmRungG`, `DispatchSwappedArmRungG`), and a `ZZ32` instantiation spelled at run time, on this path (`DispatchZZ32ArmRungG`). What else it changes: an arm in the more-specific relation that is not the dispatcher's by position is tested at the call's instantiation. For `f[\T\](x: T)` beside `f[\U\](x: Box[\U\])` reached through a generic caller, and for `grab[\Y\](t: Fixed[\Y\])` with `Fixed[\Y\] extends Tag[\Blue\]`, the compiled answer moved from the more specific arm to the less specific one (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/skeptic/dispatch-pos.txt:6`, `:17`, `:38`, `:45`). Reach: it changes no class of the compiler library's five jars (the one class that differs, `cast`'s template, is the clause-binding fix's), and the 20 sized tests' verdicts, outputs and classes are identical (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/library-jars.txt`, `compare-sized.txt`). Of the 43 generic-overload compiler tests, only the dispatcher templates of `Compiled12.invariantInference`, `invariantInference2` and `Compiled180` change, with every verdict and output the same (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/compare-generic-overload.txt`). Remainder: generic dotted methods (row 495; `compiler_tests/XXXDispatchMethodArmRungG`) and a dispatcher that is not a template (row 496) keep both defects.

The integer chapter's opening states `narrow` (the low 32 bits of a `ZZ64`, `ZZ` or `NN64`) and `LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` on the five integer types: on a fixed width `n` and a count `k >= 0`, `x RSHIFT k` is `floor(x/2^k)` and `x LSHIFT k` is `x 2^k` reduced into the type modulo `2^n`, a negative count shifting the other way, the count of any integer type read by its value, and on `ZZ` the two are `shift(x,k)` and `shift(x,-k)` (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-66`). The entry of `shift` adds that it is exact at any count and that a result too large for the implementation throws `IntegerOverflow` (`:725-730`). `GCD` and `LCM` give the absolute value of the other argument where the Working Draft said the other argument, with the property `(m GCD n)(m LCM n) = abs(m n)` (`:541-568`). The operator overview adds that both results are nonnegative and that a result a fixed-size type cannot hold throws `IntegerOverflow`, and it names the shifts among the bitwise operators (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:262-270`, `:341-344`). The coercion chapter's example declares `ZZ32 excludes { ZZ64, ZZ128 }` and `ZZ64 excludes { ZZ128 }`, as the library spells its integer exclusions, and both paths run it as printed (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:556-597`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/probes/examples/SpecZZExcl.walk.txt`, `SpecZZExcl.compiled.txt`; row 394). `QQ`'s listing extends the library's `StandardPartialOrder`, `StandardMinMax`, `AdditiveGroup` and `MultiplicativeRing` at `QQ`, with one sentence that their laws hold for the finite rationals and need not hold where 0/0 or an infinity takes part, as those of the same traits on `RR64` need not hold where a NaN takes part (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:99-101`, `:152-154`, `:224-231`). Seven callouts; Appendix I's entries "Shifts and narrowing on the integer types", "The greatest common divisor and the least common multiple", "The example of coercion resolution" and "The algebra of the rational trait" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1343-1548`), before "Passages not yet revised" and "Route C". 132 test citations the edits moved were re-anchored, 23 of them onto the lines revised in place, with no assertion changed (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/probes/reanchor/assertion-check.txt`).

For a call of a function, a method, an operator or a generic constructor that does not write its static arguments, the declaration is chosen first, as the coercion chapter's resolution chooses it, a declaration with static parameters applicable when some instance within its bounds is and compared on its declared parameter types, so a coercion never changes which declaration is chosen when one applies without it (`:54-63`); its static arguments are then inferred: a type, `nat` or `int` parameter inside a parameter type fixed by that argument by subtyping, a type parameter inside the declared return type by the expected type, a type parameter that is the whole type of parameters taking among its arguments' types and the types they coerce to the narrowest under ⪯ that all are substitutable for and its bounds permit (for numbers the narrowest type all convert into, ℤ64 for ℤ32 with ℕ32), otherwise the intersection of its upper bounds, its declared bound (`Any` if none) and what the expected type requires of the declared return type, with nothing converted; every argument admitted by substitutability, the coercions inserted statically (`:65-106`, the bound at `:89-98`); the expected type from a variable or field declaration that declares its type, an assignment to a variable whose type is declared, a declared return type, a block's last expression where no local declaration precedes it and both branches of an `if … else`, used at `f(x)`, a method invocation or an operator, with a retry without it when the result converts (`:108-134`); the converted call dispatching by subtyping to the most specific declaration applicable to the converted values (`:136-139`). A numeral whose conversions tie is read as ℤ32, or ℤ64 or ℤ by its value, in either step; a tie a non-numeral argument makes among declarations applicable only with coercion is a static error (`:170-193`, `\seclabel{numeral-default}`). - **The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model: declarations of one name may differ in their static parameters, and a declaration with static parameters is read over its instances** (`compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md`; POSITIONS, "The static-parameter sentence goes"). The Working Draft's sentence that overloads may not differ in static parameters, 2009 text (in the earliest reachable copy, `0f49d8698`) that displaced the 1.0 release's Section 15.6.1 ("For type parameters, we use their bounds as their supertypes ... may be replaced when the static type checker and the type inference engine are implemented", `Specification-1.0-frozen/fortress.1.0.pdf`), and its echo are replaced (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-120`, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:109-123`). A declaration with static parameters is applicable when some instance within its bounds is, compared on the parameter types it declares, and instantiated after the selection (`basic/overloading.tex:149-159`, `:194-205`, `:235-242`, `:365-375`). A section, "Declarations with Static Parameters" (`advanced/overloading.tex:531-651`), states the paper's three rules with the Return Type Rule over every instance, exclusion by the 2011 paper's existential reduction with instantiation exclusion (whether a bound that rules out the only static arguments at which two parameter types could meet makes them exclude each other is left open in "Passages not yet revised", the compiled checker taking that step for a named forced argument), the `GenPlainRTR` shape as "Not allowed" beside the paper's repair, and in a callout the positional rule as the compiled implementation's restriction for two declarations with as many static parameters of their own (the POPL recheck's item 1.3), and that neither implementation runs the paper's repair (rows 159 and 537), with a reordering override as its example. The coercion chapter's resolution cross-references it three times (`basic/conversions-coercions.tex:481-493`, `:555-562`, `:623-628`) and has item 16's callout on walk's choice of a coercion on the value (`:663-675`; `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXCoercionStaticRungC.fss`, `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC.fss`: compiled `f(c) = 3`, walk `4`). The implicit bound is `Any` (`basic/trait-parameters.tex:49-62`, row 412 the divergence). The naked-`Any` rule is stated against a written `Any`, as `OverloadingChecker.checkBoundAny` applies it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:430-439`); the library's `array1` pair draws no refusal, and walk applies the rule to neither (row 534). Appendix I has seven entries on the revision, the entry "Overloading with static parameters" naming the implementations' departures from its rules (rows 159, 537, 539 and 542); its introduction says that each change follows a decision of the revival, route A the first (item 23), and "Instantiation exclusion" cites the POPL 2019 paper's [Anc-Same-Trait].
